Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — Ransomware gang abuses Microsoft Teams relays to hide malicious traffic
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] DragonForce BYOVD: Huawei/Topaz/K7/ToF drivers + ABYSSWORKER load for EDR kill · [LLM] Backdoor.Turn DLL sideload via legitimate VirtualBox/DbgView host + outbound TURN · [LLM] LimitBlankPassword LSA policy modified to enable network use of blank-password accounts · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Backdoor.Turn C2 over Microsoft Teams TURN relay (3478/3479/443 to MS IP from non-Teams) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
DragonForce BYOVD: Huawei/Topaz/K7/ToF drivers + ABYSSWORKER load for EDR kill AIInstallation High
Hunts for creation or load of the specific vulnerable kernel drivers DragonForce abused in the Dec-2025 attack (HWAuidoOs2Ec.sys, wsftprm.sys CVE-2023-52271, GameDriverx64.sys CVE-2025-61155, K7RKScan.sys CVE-2025-1055) plus ABYSSWORKER masquerading as a Palo Alto driver. These are the article's named BYOVD weapons used to terminate security tooling before ransomware deployment. Rationale: All four driver filenames and the ABYSSWORKER name are directly named in Symantec/BleepingComputer's writeup plus three CVEs (CVE-2023-52271, CVE-2025-61155, CVE-2025-1055). Driver files dropped to disk + service install of the same names is high fidelity since none of these drivers belong on a fleet endpoint. Cross-checked Loldrivers project list and CVE records. Cross-checked against: • https://www.loldrivers.io/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-52271 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-1055
ATT&CKT1068 T1562.001 T1014
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Services
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate K7 Antivirus install on a managed endpoint (K7RKScan.sys is part of the K7 product)
  • Huawei laptop OEM-image deployment writing HWAuidoOs2Ec.sys
  • Tower of Fantasy game install on a corp gaming/test machine writing GameDriverx64.sys
  • Topaz signature pad driver install on a kiosk/POS host
  • Security researcher / red-team detonating loldrivers samples in a sandbox VM
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\K7 Computing" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Huawei" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Topaz Systems"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceFileEvents/DeviceImageLoadEvents for the host. Determine if the driver write/load came from a signed installer in Program Files (likely legit OEM) vs an unsigned process from a temp/Public/AppData path (suspicious). Pull SHA256 and check against LolDrivers known-bad list. 2) Contain: if path is non-standard or process is unsigned, isolate the host via Defender/Falcon network-contain, kill loaded service, block hash in EDR. 3) Hunt: pivot to the same DeviceId for outbound TURN traffic (UC4), DbgView64.exe execution (UC2), and LimitBlankPasswordUse registry write (UC3). Sweep org for the same SHA256 in DeviceFileEvents over 30d.
let DriverNames = dynamic(["hwauidoos2ec.sys","wsftprm.sys","gamedriverx64.sys","k7rkscan.sys","abyssworker"]);
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
    | where FileName has_any (DriverNames)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, Source = "FileEvent";
let LoadHits = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName has_any (DriverNames)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName = "", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, Source = "ImageLoad";
union FileHits, LoadHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let DriverNames = dynamic(["hwauidoos2ec.sys","wsftprm.sys","gamedriverx64.sys","k7rkscan.sys","abyssworker"]);
let FileHits = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
    | where TargetFileName has_any (DriverNames)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername, ActingProcess = ActingProcessName, ActingCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, FilePath = TargetFilePath, FileName = TargetFileName, Hash = TargetFileSHA256, Source = "FileEvent";
let SvcHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID in (7045, 4697)
    | where ServiceFileName has_any (DriverNames) or ServiceName has_any (DriverNames)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, User = SubjectUserName, ActingProcess = "", ActingCmd = "", FilePath = ServiceFileName, FileName = ServiceName, Hash = "", Source = "ServiceInstall";
union FileHits, SvcHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DragonForce BYOVD Driver File Created or Loaded
id: 7c4e2a91-3d6b-4f8c-9a1e-2b5d8c7e9f31
description: Detects creation or load of vulnerable drivers (HWAuidoOs2Ec.sys, wsftprm.sys, GameDriverx64.sys, K7RKScan.sys) and ABYSSWORKER used by DragonForce ransomware to disable EDR via BYOVD.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ransomware-gang-abuses-microsoft-teams-relays-to-hide-malicious-traffic/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.t1014
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows

      - '\K7RKScan.sys'

level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:(11 OR 6 OR 7045) OR @EventID:4697) (@TargetFilename:(*\HWAuidoOs2Ec.sys OR *\hwauidoos2ec.sys OR *\wsftprm.sys OR *\WSFTPRM.SYS OR *\GameDriverx64.sys OR *\gamedriverx64.sys OR *\K7RKScan.sys OR *\k7rkscan.sys OR *abyssworker*) OR @ImageLoaded:(*\HWAuidoOs2Ec.sys OR *\wsftprm.sys OR *\GameDriverx64.sys OR *\K7RKScan.sys) OR @ServiceFileName:(*HWAuidoOs2Ec* OR *wsftprm* OR *GameDriverx64* OR *K7RKScan* OR *abyssworker*))
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten OR #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate) (TargetFileName=/(hwauidoos2ec|wsftprm|gamedriverx64|k7rkscan)\.sys$/i OR ImageFileName=/(hwauidoos2ec|wsftprm|gamedriverx64|k7rkscan)\.sys$/i OR RegStringValue=/(hwauidoos2ec|wsftprm|gamedriverx64|k7rkscan|abyssworker)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, event_simpleName, TargetFileName, ImageFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
NETWORK

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created (Filesystem.file_name IN ("HWAuidoOs2Ec.sys","hwauidoos2ec.sys","wsftprm.sys","GameDriverx64.sys","gamedriverx64.sys","K7RKScan.sys","k7rkscan.sys") OR Filesystem.file_name="*abyssworker*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

Backdoor.Turn DLL sideload via legitimate VirtualBox/DbgView host + outbound TURN AIInstallation High
Hunts for execution of the legitimate signed VirtualBox or Sysinternals DbgView (specifically dbgview64.exe per the writeup) from non-Program-Files directories — the DragonForce delivery pattern where the signed host loads a malicious sideload DLL from the extracted ZIP. Also flags injection of Backdoor.Turn into dbgview64.exe. Rationale: Article specifies attacker downloaded a ZIP containing legitimate VirtualBox/DbgView + a malicious sideload DLL, and that Backdoor.Turn was injected into dbgview64.exe. Filtering signed-binary execution to non-Program-Files paths is the high-fidelity signal for portable-sideload hosts. Sysinternals/Oracle path allowlist suppresses dev workstations. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/ • https://lolbas-project.github.io/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1055 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmins running portable Sysinternals DbgView from a USB or network share for troubleshooting
  • QA team running portable VirtualBox.exe from a Downloads folder
  • Pentester / red-team using DbgView for kernel debug on a test box
  • Software developer extracting Oracle VirtualBox to a custom path
  • Vendor support engineer running VBoxManage.exe from a tool kit on a non-default path
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sccm.exe","ccmexec.exe","intune-managementextension.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Microsoft Intune Management Extension\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the parent process — legitimate runs originate from explorer.exe (user double-click) or a known IT-deploy tool; suspicious runs originate from cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or an unsigned extractor. Pull DLLs loaded by the host PID (DeviceImageLoadEvents) and check for unsigned DLLs from the same folder — classic sideload signature. 2) Contain: if a sideloaded unsigned DLL is loaded, isolate host, snapshot memory of dbgview64.exe for Backdoor.Turn IOCs, terminate the process tree. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceId to the BYOVD driver detection (UC1), to UDP/3478 TURN traffic (UC4), and to LimitBlankPasswordUse registry change (UC3). Sweep org by SHA256 of the host binary's DLL neighbours.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("dbgview.exe","dbgview64.exe","virtualbox.exe","vboxmanage.exe","vboxsvc.exe")
| where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Oracle\VirtualBox"
   and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Oracle\VirtualBox"
   and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Sysinternals"
   and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Debugging Tools"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\PerfLogs\")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dbgview64.exe","dbgview.exe","virtualbox.exe")
    | where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32" and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
    | project DeviceId, SideloadedDll = FileName, SideloadedDllPath = FolderPath, SideloadSha = SHA256
) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, HostBinary = FileName, HostPath = FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, SideloadedDll, SideloadedDllPath, SideloadSha
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("dbgview.exe","dbgview64.exe","virtualbox.exe","vboxmanage.exe","vboxsvc.exe")
| extend TargetProcessFolder = tostring(split(TargetProcessName, "\\")[0])
| where TargetProcessCommandLine !has @"C:\Program Files\Oracle\VirtualBox"
   and TargetProcessCommandLine !has @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Oracle\VirtualBox"
   and TargetProcessCommandLine !has @"C:\Program Files\Sysinternals"
   and TargetProcessCommandLine !has @"C:\Program Files\Debugging Tools"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\PerfLogs\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash = SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

LimitBlankPassword LSA policy modified to enable network use of blank-password accounts AIInstallation High
Detects modification of HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\LimitBlankPasswordUse to 0 — the article calls out DragonForce abusing this security policy to make rogue blank-password accounts usable over the network. By default Windows sets this to 1 (blank-password accounts are local-console only); flipping to 0 is a deliberate weakening of the auth boundary. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'LimitBlankPassword' Windows security policy abuse by DragonForce to make rogue users usable. Default Windows value is 1; an observed write of 0 to this specific registry path is extremely rare in a managed environment — single event is high fidelity. No CIS/STIG baseline sets this to 0. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/security-policy-settings/accounts-limit-local-account-use-of-blank-passwords-to-console-logon-only
ATT&CKT1112 T1078.003 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Misconfigured GPO from a legacy domain still pushing the value (rare)
  • Sysadmin testing local account behaviour in a lab
  • Old security baseline rollback during a misguided remediation
  • Vendor installer that incorrectly toggles the LSA policy (very rare — would be a CVE-worthy bug)
  • Manual reg.exe / Set-ItemProperty from an interactive admin troubleshooting session
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("gpsvc.exe","trustedinstaller.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !=~ "services.exe"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process — reg.exe, powershell.exe, secedit.exe under an admin session is suspicious; gpsvc.exe receiving from a legitimate GPO is benign (correlate against AD GPO change events). Check the timing against any change-management ticket. 2) Contain: revert the value to 1 via GPO or local reg push, isolate the host, audit local account creation events (4720) and group membership changes (4732/4728) on that DeviceId in the prior 24h. 3) Hunt: enumerate all local accounts with blank or weak passwords (`net user`), sweep the org for the same registry value across 30d, and pivot to UC1/UC2/UC4 detections on the same DeviceId.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "LimitBlankPasswordUse"
| where RegistryValueData == "0" or RegistryValueData == "0x0" or RegistryValueData == "0x00000000"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, PreviousRegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated","Set")
| where RegistryKey has @"\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa"
| where RegistryValue =~ "LimitBlankPasswordUse"
| where RegistryValueData in ("0", "0x0", "0x00000000")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, RegistryPreviousValueData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Backdoor.Turn C2 over Microsoft Teams TURN relay (3478/3479/443 to MS IP from non-Teams) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for the article's signature C2 channel — outbound UDP/3478-3481 or TCP/443 to Microsoft Teams TURN relay infrastructure from a process that is NOT the Teams client. Backdoor.Turn obtains an anonymous Teams visitor token and tunnels C2 through legitimate MS TURN servers, so the host process binding the socket should never be teams.exe / ms-teams.exe. Rationale: Article's central novel TTP: 'Backdoor.Turn is the first known in-the-wild malware to abuse Microsoft Teams TURN relays for C2', specifically obtaining anonymous Teams visitor tokens and connecting via legitimate MS TURN. Detection logic — non-Teams process binding to TURN ports / Teams TURN hostnames — directly maps to that. Cross-checked against Praetorian 'Ghost Calls' research which used the same primitive in 2025. Cross-checked against: • https://www.praetorian.com/blog/ghost-calls-abusing-web-conferencing-infrastructure/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/prepare-network • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/002/
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1102.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom enterprise VoIP/SIP client legitimately using STUN/TURN on 3478
  • WebRTC-based apps (Slack Huddles, Zoom, Discord) traversing 3478 to non-Microsoft TURN servers — usually filterable but watch RemoteUrl
  • Internal NAT-traversal tooling used by remote-access products (TeamViewer, AnyDesk) when they fall back to STUN
  • Browsers (chrome.exe, msedge.exe) running Teams web client — should still be filtered by hostname/Teams cookie path but can be noisy
  • Network test tools (stuntman, coturn-client) used by network engineers
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("slack.exe","zoom.exe","discord.exe","webex.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\TeamViewer\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\AnyDesk\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the initiating process binary, its SHA256, signing status, and folder. Legitimate Teams traffic always originates from Teams.exe under Program Files\WindowsApps or Microsoft\Teams\current; any other process bound to 3478 is the lead. Decode the visitor-token request (HTTPS to *.teams.microsoft.com/anonymousjoin) in proxy logs if available. 2) Contain: network-isolate the host, dump memory of the suspect process for Go-runtime strings (RAT was Go-based per article) and TURN credentials, block the C2 destination IP at the perimeter. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceId to UC2 (dbgview64.exe) and UC1 (BYOVD drivers) — if those fire on the same host, treat as confirmed DragonForce. Sweep org for the same destination IP/hostname pattern over 30d and for processes that issued TURN allocation requests but lack a teams.exe parent.
let TURNPorts = dynamic([3478,3479,3480,3481]);
let TeamsBinaries = dynamic(["teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","msteams.exe","microsoft.teams.exe"]);
let TeamsHosts = dynamic(["turn.teams.microsoft.com","worldaz.tr.teams.microsoft.com","relay.teams.microsoft.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt")
| where (Protocol =~ "Udp" and RemotePort in (TURNPorts))
   or (RemotePort == 443 and (RemoteUrl has_any (TeamsHosts) or RemoteUrl endswith ".teams.cloud.microsoft"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (TeamsBinaries)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Microsoft\Teams\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\WindowsApps\MSTeams"
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Ports = make_set(RemotePort), DistinctRemotes = dcount(RemoteIP), SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by ConnCount desc
let TURNPorts = dynamic([3478,3479,3480,3481]);
let TeamsBinaries = dynamic(["teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","msteams.exe","microsoft.teams.exe"]);
let TeamsHostnames = dynamic(["turn.teams.microsoft.com","worldaz.tr.teams.microsoft.com","relay.teams.microsoft.com"]);
let TeamsRunningHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetProcessName has_any (TeamsBinaries)
    | summarize TeamsLastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (NetworkProtocol =~ "UDP" and DstPortNumber in (TURNPorts))
   or (DstPortNumber == 443 and (DstHostname has_any (TeamsHostnames) or DstHostname endswith ".teams.cloud.microsoft"))
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Ports = make_set(DstPortNumber), DistinctRemotes = dcount(DstIpAddr), SampleRemote = any(DstIpAddr), SampleHostname = any(DstHostname)
          by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr
| join kind=leftouter TeamsRunningHosts on DvcHostname
| where isempty(TeamsLastSeen) or LastSeen > TeamsLastSeen + 1h
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, ConnCount, Ports, DistinctRemotes, SampleRemote, SampleHostname, TeamsLastSeen
| order by ConnCount desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:3 (@DestinationPort:(3478 OR 3479 OR 3480 OR 3481) OR (@DestinationPort:443 AND @DestinationHostname:(*.teams.microsoft.com OR *.teams.cloud.microsoft OR worldaz.tr.teams.microsoft.com))) -@Image:(*\teams.exe OR *\Teams.exe OR *\ms-teams.exe OR *\msteams.exe OR *\Microsoft.Teams.exe) -@Image:(*\Microsoft\Teams\* OR *\WindowsApps\MSTeams*)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemotePort=3478 OR RemotePort=3479 OR RemotePort=3480 OR RemotePort=3481 OR (RemotePort=443 AND ContextImageFileName!=/\\(teams|ms-teams|msteams)\.exe$/i))
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(teams|ms-teams|msteams|Microsoft\.Teams)\.exe$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(Microsoft\\Teams|WindowsApps\\MSTeams)\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count(as=ConnCount))
| ConnCount >= 3
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port values(All_Traffic.transport) as transport from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_port IN (3478,3479,3480,3481) OR (All_Traffic.dest_port=443 AND (All_Traffic.dest="*.teams.microsoft.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.teams.cloud.microsoft" OR All_Traffic.dest="worldaz.tr.teams.microsoft.com"))) NOT All_Traffic.app IN ("teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","msteams.exe","Microsoft.Teams.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port values(All_Traffic.transport) as transport from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_port IN (3478,3479,3480,3481) OR (All_Traffic.dest_port=443 AND (All_Traffic.dest="*.teams.microsoft.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.teams.cloud.microsoft" OR All_Traffic.dest="worldaz.tr.teams.microsoft.com"))) NOT All_Traffic.app IN ("teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","msteams.exe","Microsoft.Teams.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("62.164.177.25", "192.36.27.51") or RemoteUrl has_any ("projetosmecanicos.com.br", "socialbizsolutions.com", "professionalhomebasedbusiness.com", "safefire.jo", "glanz-gmbh.de", "turnkeyaiagents.com", "comunidadesparentais.com.br", "mysimerp.net")

let BadIPs     = dynamic(["62.164.177.25", "192.36.27.51"]);

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/

tags:

            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'

    selection_domain:

            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'

falsepositives:

level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("projetosmecanicos.com.br", "socialbizsolutions.com", "professionalhomebasedbusiness.com", "safefire.jo", "glanz-gmbh.de", "turnkeyaiagents.com", "comunidadesparentais.com.br", "mysimerp.net")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("62.164.177.25", "192.36.27.51")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("projetosmecanicos.com.br", "socialbizsolutions.com", "professionalhomebasedbusiness.com", "safefire.jo", "glanz-gmbh.de", "turnkeyaiagents.com", "comunidadesparentais.com.br", "mysimerp.net")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user

        where DNS.query IN ("projetosmecanicos.com.br", "socialbizsolutions.com", "professionalhomebasedbusiness.com", "safefire.jo", "glanz-gmbh.de", "turnkeyaiagents.com", "comunidadesparentais.com.br", "mysimerp.net")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-52271", "CVE-2025-61155", "CVE-2025-1055")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-52271", "CVE-2025-61155", "CVE-2025-1055")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2023-52271", "CVE-2025-61155", "CVE-2025-1055")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2023-52271", "CVE-2025-61155", "CVE-2025-1055")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027

union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical

Vulnerable google-cloud-aiplatform SDK install (CVE-2026-2473 — pre-1.148.0) AIWeaponization High
Detects installation or invocation of google-cloud-aiplatform Python SDK at versions 1.139.0 through 1.147.x, which silently fall back to an attacker-owned GCS bucket via the deterministic `<project>-vertex-staging-<location>` pattern when no explicit staging bucket is supplied. Catches both first-time installs and runtime use of vulnerable libraries that should be upgraded to ≥1.148.0. Rationale: Pins to the EXACT vulnerable SDK version range disclosed in the Unit 42 article (1.139.0 — 1.147.x; fixed in 1.148.0 released 2026-04-15). The version regex eliminates noise from already-patched installs. Catches both interactive pip installs and CI/CD pipelines pulling pinned vulnerable versions. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/hijacking-vertex-ai-model/ • https://pypi.org/project/google-cloud-aiplatform/#history
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Data science teams legitimately running pinned but outdated SDK versions in research notebooks
  • CI/CD pipelines re-installing an old pinned version in lockfiles awaiting upgrade
  • Docker image rebuilds replaying historical pip install commands from cached layers
  • Developers reproducing a known issue against a specific old SDK version for support tickets
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("docker.exe","buildkitd.exe") and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dry-run","download","--no-deps"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host/user and pull the full pip-install context — is this a developer workstation, build agent, or production ML pipeline? Check whether the SDK is actively used (search for `aiplatform.Model.upload` calls in the same project). 2) Contain: force-upgrade google-cloud-aiplatform to ≥1.148.0 in the affected environment; if the host has uploaded models in the last 7 days, treat any default-named staging buckets as suspect and verify ownership via `gcloud storage buckets describe`. 3) Hunt: pivot to GCS audit logs for any bucket matching `<project-id>-vertex-staging-<location>` and confirm the bucket resides in the customer's own project, not an attacker-controlled one. Check Vertex AI Model Registry for models uploaded during the vulnerable window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "google-cloud-aiplatform"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"google-cloud-aiplatform==1\.(139|140|141|142|143|144|145|146|147)\."
| extend VulnerableVersion = extract(@"google-cloud-aiplatform==(1\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountUpn, VulnerableVersion, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "pip.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "pip3.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "python.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "python3.exe"
| where CommandLine has "google-cloud-aiplatform"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"google-cloud-aiplatform==1\.(139|140|141|142|143|144|145|146|147)\."
| extend VulnerableVersion = extract(@"google-cloud-aiplatform==(1\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, CommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, VulnerableVersion, CommandLine, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vertex AI default staging bucket squatting — predictable bucket pattern access AIDelivery Medium
Hunts GCP audit logs for storage operations on buckets matching the deterministic `<project-id>-vertex-staging-<location>` pattern where the acting identity is NOT the customer's Vertex AI P4SA (`service-<project-num>@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com`) or a known internal pipeline service account. Surfaces both cross-tenant bucket squatting and unexpected writes that could be model-artifact poisoning. Rationale: Targets the exact bucket-name pattern from the article (`staging_bucket_name = project + "-vertex-staging-" + location`). Filtering OUT the legitimate Vertex AI P4SA isolates the access path the attacker would use — either bucket-squatting from a different project or an unexpected internal principal touching the staging bucket. Sigma omitted because this requires aggregation/exclusion logic not expressible as single-event-shape. Falcon/Defender/CloudWatch empty because this is GCP-native telemetry with no Falcon FDR or Microsoft endpoint equivalent. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/hijacking-vertex-ai-model/ • https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-agents
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1525 T1530
Data sourcesWeb Change
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Customer DevOps service account legitimately reading the staging bucket during pipeline orchestration
  • Terraform/IaC service account creating or auditing the bucket during infra provisioning
  • Cloud Storage Transfer Service or Backup service principals enumerating buckets
  • Internal user using `gcloud storage` CLI for ad-hoc model artifact inspection
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm bucket ownership with `gcloud storage buckets describe gs://<bucket>` — if the project_number doesn't match your project, you've been squatted; treat as confirmed. Inventory any model artifacts already staged there. 2) Contain: immediately delete and recreate the bucket explicitly under your project, then upgrade the SDK to ≥1.148.0 across all clients. Revoke any models uploaded during the vulnerable window from the Vertex AI Model Registry and redeploy from a verified source. 3) Hunt: pull Vertex AI deployment events for the affected region and inspect model artifacts (`gsutil cat gs://<bucket>/.../model.joblib | python -c 'import pickletools; pickletools.dis(...)'`) for `__reduce__` payloads. Check IAM audit logs for any new permissions granted to external principals.
GCPAuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ServiceName == "storage.googleapis.com"
| extend BucketName = extract(@"projects/_/buckets/([^/]+)", 1, tostring(ResourceName))
| where BucketName matches regex @"-vertex-staging-(us|europe|asia|australia|northamerica|southamerica)"
| extend Principal = tostring(AuthenticationInfo.principalEmail)
| where Principal !endswith "@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Methods=make_set(MethodName), Principals=make_set(Principal), EventCount=count() by BucketName
| order by LastSeen desc
source:gcp.audit @protoPayload.serviceName:storage.googleapis.com @protoPayload.resourceName:*-vertex-staging-* -@protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:*@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com
CLOUD
`gcp_audit_logs` data.protoPayload.serviceName="storage.googleapis.com"
| rex field=data.protoPayload.resourceName "projects/_/buckets/(?<bucket_name>[^/]+)"
| where match(bucket_name, "-vertex-staging-(us|europe|asia|australia|northamerica|southamerica)")
| eval principal=data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail
| where NOT match(principal, "gcp-sa-aiplatform\.iam\.gserviceaccount\.com$")
| stats min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(data.protoPayload.methodName) as methods values(principal) as principals count by bucket_name
| `security_content_ctime(firstSeen)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastSeen)`

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

China-Linked SprySOCKS Backdoor Expands to Windows with Driver-Based Stealth

The Hacker News
2026-06-16 7 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have flagged two previously undocumented Windows variants of what was believed to be a Linux-only backdoor called SprySOCKS. "The Windows variants discovered are internally marked as WIN_DRV and WIN_PLUS," ESET said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "Both come with a hard-coded C&amp;C [command-and-control] configuration and support communication over TCP, UDP,

Print Spooler (spoolsv.exe) spawning svchost.exe child — SprySOCKS WIN_PLUS print-processor loader AIInstallation High
Hunts the WIN_PLUS execution chain where the Windows Print Spooler service is abused to load a first-stage loader as a print processor, which then injects the SprySOCKS loader into a newly spawned svchost.exe. spoolsv.exe spawning svchost.exe is not legitimate Windows behaviour and is the WIN_PLUS-specific pivot called out in the ESET write-up. Rationale: spoolsv.exe is never the legitimate parent of svchost.exe — svchost is started by services.exe with -k <svcgroup>. ESET's WIN_PLUS chain explicitly stages the SprySOCKS loader into a freshly created svchost child of spoolsv via a malicious print processor, making this parent/child pair article-specific and very low-FP. Cross-checked T1547.012 Print Processors technique mapping on MITRE ATT&CK. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/012/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1055/012/
ATT&CKT1547.012 T1055.012
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Third-party print driver bundles (HP / Konica / Lexmark) that occasionally spawn helper svchost-like processes during driver install
  • Print spooler crash + WER svchost handoff during fault recovery on legacy hardware
  • Custom EDR/AV print monitoring helpers using svchost.exe as an invocation stub
  • Patch test labs running the spooler under a service-host harness
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\system32\\" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"-k\s+\w+")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the svchost child's process tree and command line plus the print processor DLL loaded by spoolsv in the 60s preceding the spawn (DeviceImageLoadEvents on the same DeviceId). Hash-check the loaded DLL and verify Authenticode — a SprySOCKS print processor will be unsigned or signed by an unknown CA. Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill the spoolsv-spawned svchost, and remove the malicious print processor value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Environments\Windows x64\Print Processors. Hunt: pivot on the loader DLL hash across the org, look for kernel-driver service registrations matching UC2, and review egress for TCP/UDP/WebSocket callbacks from the injected svchost.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "spoolsv.exe"
| where FileName =~ "svchost.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine !contains "-k "
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\spoolsv.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\svchost.exe"
| where CommandLine !contains "-k "
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, NewProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Kernel driver service registered with .dat image path (SprySOCKS DriverLoader pattern) AIInstallation High
Detects creation of a Windows kernel-mode driver service whose ImagePath references a .dat file — matching the SprySOCKS WIN_DRV pattern where the encrypted DriverLoader (KX1B5206BDC1743DD.dat) loads the RawWNPF rootkit driver (KW1B5206BDC1743FP.dat). Legitimate kernel drivers ship as .sys, so a kernel service with a .dat image is highly anomalous. Rationale: Legitimate kernel-mode drivers ship as .sys; an ImagePath ending in .dat combined with ServiceType kernel/filesystem is highly anomalous. ESET disclosed the exact filenames (KX1B5206BDC1743DD.dat DriverLoader, KW1B5206BDC1743FP.dat RawWNPF) so the regex anchors on the SprySOCKS naming pattern while still catching naming-scheme variants. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1014/
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1014
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor utilities that ship encrypted blobs renamed .dat and load them via a kernel driver (rare; some EDR/sandbox vendors)
  • Legacy backup or VPN clients that historically registered a kernel-mode helper with a .dat config path
  • Custom in-house driver development on engineering workstations using non-standard extensions
  • Anti-cheat or DRM drivers using .dat container files for the kernel image
Suppression filter
and not ServiceFileName has_any ("\\program files\\", "\\program files (x86)\\")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the ServiceFileName from disk, capture SHA256 plus Authenticode signing details and check whether the file lives outside %SystemRoot%\System32\drivers — an unsigned .dat in a writable directory is a near-certain rootkit. Contain: stop and delete the service via Defender Live Response, quarantine the .dat file, and snapshot memory for the loaded driver before reboot to preserve kernel state. Hunt: pivot org-wide on the filename pattern KW1B5206BDC1743FP.dat / KX1B5206BDC1743DD.dat and on the resulting SHA256; look for scheduled tasks dropped in the prior 24h and for the WIN_PLUS spoolsv→svchost chain in UC1 on adjacent hosts.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "ServiceInstalled"
| extend Extra = parse_json(AdditionalFields)
| extend ImagePath = tostring(Extra.ServiceFileName)
| extend SvcType = tostring(Extra.ServiceType)
| where ImagePath endswith ".dat"
   or ImagePath matches regex @"K[WX]1B5206BDC1743[A-Z0-9]{2}\.dat"
| where SvcType has_any ("KernelModeDriver", "FileSystemDriver", "1", "2") or isempty(SvcType)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ImagePath, SvcType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4697
| where ServiceType has_any ("kernel mode driver", "file system driver", "0x1", "0x2")
| where ServiceFileName has ".dat"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ServiceName, ServiceFileName, ServiceType, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SprySOCKS WIN_DRV component .dat filenames written to disk (RawWNPF / DriverLoader) AIInstallation High
Hunts file-write events for the hard-coded SprySOCKS WIN_DRV driver-component filenames disclosed by ESET — KW1B5206BDC1743FP.dat (RawWNPF rootkit driver) and KX1B5206BDC1743DD.dat (encrypted DriverLoader). Any match is a high-confidence indicator of WIN_DRV deployment. Rationale: Filenames are hard-coded SprySOCKS WIN_DRV components disclosed in ESET's report. No legitimate software ships files matching the K[WX]1B5206BDC1743**.dat pattern; the regex anchors catch sibling variants under the same naming convention. Any hit is investigate-immediately. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1014/
ATT&CKT1014 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-research sandbox detonation environments storing malware samples with original filenames preserved
  • Forensic image acquisition tooling unpacking IR evidence on a managed endpoint
  • Security analyst downloading the ESET IOC bundle to their workstation
  • Honeypot or deception VMs intentionally seeded with these filenames for canary alerting
Suppression filter
and not FolderPath has_any ("\\sandbox\\", "\\malware-samples\\", "\\ir-evidence\\", "\\quarantine\\")
Response runbook
Triage: capture SHA256 of the dropped file and the InitiatingProcess that wrote it; cross-check against VirusTotal and ESET — a confirmed hash match is a critical incident requiring no further triage. Contain: isolate the host, kill the writing process tree, quarantine the file, and capture memory before reboot to preserve the kernel-driver state for forensics. Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessSHA256 of the loader across the org, look for the scheduled task that triggered the DLL side-loading chain in the prior 24h, hunt for the kernel-driver service registration (UC2) and the spoolsv→svchost chain (UC1), and review egress for TCP/UDP/WebSocket callbacks from svchost/spoolsv lineage.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where FileName in~ ("KW1B5206BDC1743FP.dat", "KX1B5206BDC1743DD.dat")
   or FileName matches regex @"^K[WX]1B5206BDC1743[A-Z0-9]{2}\.dat$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("KW1B5206BDC1743FP.dat", "KX1B5206BDC1743DD.dat")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
