  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  product: cisco_sdwan
  service: vmanage_appserver
detection:
  selection:
    Message|contains: 'WFLYSRV0010: Deployed'
  filter_baseline:
    Message|contains:
      - 'vmanage.war'
      - 'configuration.war'
      - 'olap.war'
      - 'scheduler.war'
      - 'statistics-app.war'
      - 'sdwan-portal.war'
  condition: selection and not filter_baseline
falsepositives:
  - Cisco-pushed package update introducing a new WAR (rare, coincides with version bump)
level: high
source:cisco.sdwan "WFLYSRV0010: Deployed" -"vmanage.war" -"configuration.war" -"olap.war" -"scheduler.war" -"statistics-app.war" -"sdwan-portal.war"
APPLICATION
search index=cisco_sdwan source="/var/log/nms/vmanage-appserver.log" "WFLYSRV0010: Deployed"
| rex field=_raw "WFLYSRV0010:\s+Deployed\s+.(?<war_name>\S+?\.war)"
| where isnotnull(war_name) AND NOT match(war_name, "^(vmanage|configuration|olap|scheduler|statistics|sdwan).*\.war$")
| stats min(_time) as first_seen, count, values(war_name) as war_files by host
| where first_seen >= relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
vManage service-proxy POST to attacker-deployed JSP webshell AICommand & Control High
Detects POST requests landing on a JSP path served by the vManage service-proxy that is not part of the legitimate vManage application context. After CVE-2026-20262 exploitation drops a WAR and Wildfly deploys it, the attacker interacts with index.jsp via HTTP POST through service-proxy — surfacing as a serviceproxy-access.log entry referencing the rogue context root. Rationale: Anchored on the literal access-log shape from the article: '"POST /suspicious/index.jsp HTTP/1.1" 200'. The vManage application context roots are well-known (login, app, portal, home, dataservice) and any POST to a JSP outside that set indicates an attacker-deployed web shell. Joining this UC with the WFLYSRV0010 'Deployed' UC by the same context root gives a deterministic exploit-to-interaction signal. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sdwan-arbfw-c2rZvQ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/cisco-sd-wan-vmanage-vulnerability-exploit/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cisco SD-WAN upgrade introducing a new context root containing legitimate JSP endpoints (catch via version-correlated allowlist update)
  • Customer-deployed custom dashboard WAR with its own JSP (rare; would be tracked via change-management)
  • Penetration test or red-team exercise against the vManage by an authorised engagement
  • Misconfigured WAF/loadbalancer health check that probes a non-standard JSP path with a POST
Suppression filter
and not (UriPath matches regex @"^/(?:dataservice|management)/[a-z0-9_/-]+/[a-z0-9_-]+\.jsp$")
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the JSP path, source IP, and request-id from the access log; correlate the same request-id back to vmanage-appserver.log to find which WAR served the request; pull the response status and bytes. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the edge firewall, undeploy the offending WAR (rm /var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/<war>.deployed), snapshot the appliance, rotate vManage admin and netadmin credentials, force re-onboarding of any edge router whose template was modified in the same window. 3) Hunt: pivot on source IP across all vManage cluster nodes, search for outbound connections initiated by the wildfly java process to non-management IPs (vmanage normally only talks to controllers/validators), review NMS audit log for any template/policy push by the compromised session.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "POST" and SyslogMessage has ".jsp"
| extend UriPath = extract(@"POST\s+(/\S+\.jsp)\s+HTTP", 1, SyslogMessage)
| where isnotempty(UriPath)
| where not(UriPath matches regex @"^/(login|app|portal|home|static|dataservice)/")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), Count = count(), JspPaths = make_set(UriPath) by Computer
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Cisco vManage Service-Proxy POST to JSP Web Shell (CVE-2026-20262)
id: 8b6caf43-3e4f-6cb1-bd43-509e7f9b3456
description: Detects HTTP POST requests to JSP paths on the vManage service-proxy that are not part of the legitimate application context — indicates web-shell interaction following CVE-2026-20262 exploitation.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/cisco-releases-security-updates-for.html
  - https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sdwan-arbfw-c2rZvQ
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:

  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  product: cisco_sdwan
  service: serviceproxy_access
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: 'POST'
    cs-uri-stem|endswith: '.jsp'
  filter_legit:

      - '/login/'
      - '/app/'
      - '/portal/'
      - '/home/'
      - '/dataservice/'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Cisco-internal diagnostic JSP under a new context root (rare, ties to version upgrade)
level: high
source:cisco.sdwan @http.method:POST @http.url:*.jsp -@http.url:(/login/* OR /app/* OR /portal/* OR /home/* OR /dataservice/*)
APPLICATION
search index=cisco_sdwan source="/var/log/nms/containers/service-proxy/serviceproxy-access.log" "POST" ".jsp"
| rex field=_raw "POST\s+(?<uri_path>/\S+\.jsp)\s+HTTP"
| where isnotnull(uri_path) AND NOT match(uri_path, "^/(login|app|portal|home|static|dataservice)/")
| stats min(_time) as first_seen, count, dc(src) as unique_sources, values(uri_path) as jsp_paths by host
| where first_seen >= relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

CVE-2026-54420 LiteSpeed cPanel exploit: generateEcCert chained to packageUserSize for same user AIExploitation High
Detects the specific exploitation pattern for CVE-2026-54420 where an attacker with FTP/web shell access on a CloudLinux/CageFS shared host invokes the cPanel JSON API function `generateEcCert` immediately followed by `packageUserSize` for the same cPanel user within seconds. LiteSpeed explicitly states legitimate UI flows never chain these two calls — this is the highest-fidelity signature published by the vendor. Rationale: Anchored on the EXACT IOC strings published by LiteSpeed in the article body (`cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert`, `cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize`, `cert_action_entry.*geneccert`) and the vendor's explicit statement that legitimate UI flows never chain these two calls for the same user. The 10-second correlation window is generous; LiteSpeed says the calls are 'immediately' chained, so most true positives will be sub-second. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-54420
ATT&CKT1068 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Hosting provider's own automation tool (e.g. WHM bulk-provisioning script) that legitimately issues both API calls for the same user during account setup
  • Custom reseller tooling that wraps cPanel API for SSL cert provisioning and disk-quota reporting in one workflow
  • Load-testing or QA suite hammering both API endpoints
  • Migration utility (e.g. transfer_tool) that batches per-user operations
  • cPanel auto-renewal cron job if it has been customised to also report user disk usage in the same flow
Suppression filter
| where User !in~ ("root", "cpanel", "nobody") and User !startswith "_" // exclude system-context calls
| where SrcIp !in ("127.0.0.1", "::1") // exclude localhost (WHM UI proxies through loopback in some configs)
Response runbook
1) Triage: Pull the offending log lines via the LiteSpeed grep command on the affected server and confirm the chain is for ONE cPanel user (legitimate concurrent admin work would span many). Check `whoami`/`id` history and recent root-owned file creations under /home/<user>. 2) Contain: Immediately upgrade the LiteSpeed WHM Plugin to v5.3.2.1+ (bundles cPanel plugin v2.4.8). If patching is blocked, suspend the implicated cPanel user account and any FTP credentials. Snapshot the box for forensics before remediation. 3) Hunt: Search for new root-owned binaries, modified /etc/passwd or /etc/sudoers, new SSH keys in /root/.ssh, and outbound C2 from the host since the first observation. Pivot on SrcIp across other tenants of the shared host.
// Defender XDR does not natively ingest cPanel access logs. This query targets MDE-for-Linux hosts where cPanel logs are forwarded into /var/log via rsyslog and surfaced through DeviceEvents AdditionalFields, OR detects an admin running the LiteSpeed verification grep on a potentially-compromised server.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("cpanel","whm","cloudlinux") or FolderPath has "/usr/local/cpanel/"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("grep","cpanel_jsonapi_func") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("generateEcCert","packageUserSize","geneccert")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 1d;
let WindowSec = 10;
let GenCalls = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where SyslogMessage has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert"
    | extend User = coalesce(extract(@"cpanel_jsonapi_user=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"cpanel_jsonuser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"\suser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage))
    | extend SrcIp = extract(@"((?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3})", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | project GenTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, User, SrcIp, GenMsg = SyslogMessage;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where SyslogMessage has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize"
| extend User = coalesce(extract(@"cpanel_jsonapi_user=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"cpanel_jsonuser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"\suser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage))
| join kind=inner GenCalls on Computer, User
| where TimeGenerated between (GenTime .. GenTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, GenTime)
| project FirstCall_generateEcCert = GenTime, SecondCall_packageUserSize = TimeGenerated, DelaySec, Computer, User, SrcIp, GenMsg, PackageMsg = SyslogMessage
| order by FirstCall_generateEcCert desc

CVE-2026-54420 LiteSpeed cPanel exploit: burst of 7-10 concurrent generateEcCert / packageUserSize calls AIExploitation High
Detects the second IOC LiteSpeed published for CVE-2026-54420 exploitation: 7-10 concurrent calls to the vulnerable cPanel JSON API functions per exploitation attempt. The legitimate UI invokes these one at a time, so a sudden burst from a single source IP or for a single cPanel user is the exploit's race-condition trigger. Rationale: Anchored on LiteSpeed's second published IOC in the article: '7-10 concurrent calls per attempt (legitimate UI does one at a time)'. The 5-second bucket plus the 7-20 lower/upper bound directly encodes the vendor's stated exploit signature — tight enough to avoid normal cPanel UI flows, wide enough to catch attempts that issue slightly more or fewer parallel calls. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-54420
ATT&CKT1068 T1499.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Bulk SSL certificate renewal job (e.g. Let's Encrypt sweep across many cPanel users) hitting the same WHM server in parallel
  • Reseller migration tool issuing parallel API calls during a tenant transfer
  • Load test or synthetic monitoring against the WHM API
  • cPanel high-availability replication tooling that fans out per-user calls
  • Pen-test or vulnerability-scanner sweep replaying the published PoC against the box
Suppression filter
| where User != "" and User !in~ ("root", "cpanel", "nobody", "system") // exclude background system jobs
| where DistinctApis >= 1 // at least one of the two functions was hit
| where SrcIp != "127.0.0.1" // exclude localhost (WHM UI loopback)
Response runbook
1) Triage: Confirm whether the concurrent calls are for ONE cPanel user (exploit) or many users (likely bulk-renewal cron). Cross-reference SrcIp with known WHM admin IPs; check for the same SrcIp also hitting `generateEcCert` followed by `packageUserSize` (UC #1) for a higher-fidelity confirm. 2) Contain: Upgrade LiteSpeed WHM Plugin to v5.3.2.1+ immediately (CISA deadline is 2026-06-18). If unable to patch, block the offending SrcIp at the perimeter and suspend the implicated cPanel user pending review. 3) Hunt: Look for root-owned artefacts created in user home directories post-burst, new SUID binaries, modifications to /etc/cron.d/, and unexpected symlinks under /home/*/public_html pointing outside CageFS. Sweep all cPanel users for FTP credentials that may have been used as the initial foothold.
// Defender XDR does not ingest cPanel access logs. This query hunts MDE-for-Linux hosts where cPanel JSON API calls leak into DeviceEvents AdditionalFields via syslog forwarding, or detects the LiteSpeed verification grep being executed.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("generateEcCert", "packageUserSize", "cert_action_entry")
| extend ApiFunc = case(AdditionalFields has "generateEcCert", "generateEcCert", AdditionalFields has "packageUserSize", "packageUserSize", "cert_action_entry_geneccert")
| summarize ConcurrentCalls = count(), DistinctApis = dcount(ApiFunc), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5s)
| where ConcurrentCalls >= 7
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert", "cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize") or (SyslogMessage has "cert_action_entry" and SyslogMessage has "geneccert")
| extend User = coalesce(extract(@"cpanel_jsonapi_user=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"cpanel_jsonuser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage))
| extend SrcIp = extract(@"((?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3})", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend ApiFunc = case(SyslogMessage has "generateEcCert", "generateEcCert", SyslogMessage has "packageUserSize", "packageUserSize", "cert_action_entry_geneccert")
| summarize ConcurrentCalls = count(), DistinctApis = dcount(ApiFunc), CallTypes = make_set(ApiFunc), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, User, SrcIp, bin_time = bin(TimeGenerated, 5s)
| where ConcurrentCalls between (7 .. 20) // LiteSpeed-published exploit signature: 7-10 concurrent calls per attempt
| order by bin_time desc
source:linux.syslog ("cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert" OR "cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize" OR ("cert_action_entry" "geneccert"))
#event_simpleName=/^(ProcessRollup2|SyntheticProcessRollup2)$/ | CommandLine=/cpanel_jsonapi_func=(generateEcCert|packageUserSize)/i OR CommandLine=/cert_action_entry.*geneccert/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, bucket=1s], function=count(as=concurrent_calls)) | concurrent_calls >= 7 | concurrent_calls <= 20
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.uri_query="*cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert*" OR Web.uri_query="*cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize*" OR Web.uri_query="*cert_action_entry*geneccert*") by _time Web.dest Web.src Web.user span=2s
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| where count >= 7 AND count <= 20
| stats max(count) as peak_concurrent sum(count) as total_calls values(user) as users earliest(_time) as first_seen latest(_time) as last_seen by dest src
| where peak_concurrent >= 7
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.uri_query="*cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert*" OR Web.uri_query="*cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize*" OR Web.uri_query="*cert_action_entry*geneccert*") by _time Web.dest Web.src Web.user span=2s

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/

            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'

    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:

      cross-shell escaping

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

SimpleHelp bug lets hackers create rogue remote support accounts

BleepingComputer
2026-06-15 8 use cases 1 technique 6 kill-chain phases detected

A vulnerability in the SimpleHelp remote management software allows unauthenticated attackers to create privileged technician accounts on servers using the OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication protocol. [...]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Internet-exposed SimpleHelp servers vulnerable to CVE-2026-48558 · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Rogue SimpleHelp Technician account created via OIDC bypass (CVE-2026-48558) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — SimpleHelp bug lets hackers create rogue remote support accounts
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] SimpleHelp 'Remote Access.exe' spawning script interpreters on managed endpoints · [LLM] Newly created SimpleHelp Technician immediately exercises privileged actions
Rogue SimpleHelp Technician account created via OIDC bypass (CVE-2026-48558) AIInstallation High
Detects new Technician account registrations/logons in the SimpleHelp server audit log forwarded as syslog. Targets the exact persistence vector from CVE-2026-48558 where forged OIDC identity assertions register an attacker-controlled privileged Technician without MFA. Rationale: Article explicitly names /opt/SimpleHelp/logs/server.log as the audit trail that records 'technician registrations, email addresses, and configuration changes performed by rogue accounts'. Cross-checked with Horizon3.ai disclosure which calls out IoC review focused on 'new authenticated technician users with unknown or suspicious names and/or email addresses' and confirms OIDC is the bypassed code path. Cross-checked against: • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/ • https://www.securityweek.com/vulnerabilities-in-simplehelp-remote-access-software-may-lead-to-system-compromise/
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1078.004 T1556.006
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate new MSP technician onboarded via OIDC SSO and provisioned just-in-time
  • IT bulk-imports staff into a new SimpleHelp Technician Group on first OIDC rollout
  • Test/QA Technician accounts spun up for SimpleHelp version 5.5.16 upgrade verification
  • Existing technician's UPN changes after a HR rename (creates 'new' OIDC identity)
Suppression filter
| where not (NewUser in ("", "system") or Email endswith "@yourcorp.com")
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full server.log block for the new Technician: capture username, email domain, OIDC subject claim, source IP, Technician Group joined, and whether 'Allow group authenticated logins' is enabled on that group; cross-check the username/email against HR/IdP directory. 2) Contain — if the user is not in the IdP directory or the source IP is foreign, immediately disable the Technician account in SimpleHelp, revoke any active sessions, IP-allowlist Technician logins, and verify the server is on 5.5.16 / 6.0RC2 (patch CVE-2026-48558). 3) Hunt — pivot on the same source IP/UA across server.log for prior OIDC probes; review session history for managed-endpoint remote-control or script-execution actions launched by the rogue Technician within the next 24h (feeds UC4).
let LookbackDays = 7d;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ProcessName has "SimpleHelp" or SyslogMessage has "SimpleHelp"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("Technician", "technician")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("created", "registered", "added", "OIDC login", "new technician")
| extend NewUser = extract(@"(?i)technician[^\w]+([\w._-]+@?[\w._-]*)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend Email = extract(@"([\w._%+-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend OidcFlag = iff(SyslogMessage has "OIDC" or SyslogMessage has "openid", "oidc", "other")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, Facility, OidcFlag, NewUser, Email, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:simplehelp (@message:*Technician* OR @message:*technician*) (@message:*created* OR @message:*registered* OR @message:*added* OR @message:*"OIDC login"*) (@message:*OIDC* OR @message:*openid*)
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Authentication.src) as src values(Authentication.user) as user values(Authentication.signature) as signature from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="SimpleHelp" (Authentication.signature IN ("TechnicianCreated","TechnicianRegistered","OIDCLogin","technician_added") OR Authentication.action="success") Authentication.authentication_method="OIDC" by Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where firstSeen >= relative_time(now(),"-7d") | eval suspicious=if(match(user, "(?i)(test|admin[0-9]+|temp|qa|root|svc)") OR len(user)<4 OR match(user,"^[a-z0-9]{8,}$"),1,0)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Authentication.src) as src values(Authentication.user) as user values(Authentication.signature) as signature from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="SimpleHelp" (Authentication.signature IN ("TechnicianCreated","TechnicianRegistered","OIDCLogin","technician_added") OR Authentication.action="success") Authentication.authentication_method="OIDC" by Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where firstSeen >= relative_time(now(),"-7d") | eval suspicious=if(match(user, "(?i)(test|admin[0-9]+|temp|qa|root|svc)") OR len(user)<4 OR match(user,"^[a-z0-9]{8,}$"),1,0)
SimpleHelp 'Remote Access.exe' spawning script interpreters on managed endpoints AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the post-exploitation pivot from CVE-2026-48558: a rogue Technician using SimpleHelp's 'execute scripts' capability against managed endpoints. Looks for the SimpleHelp customer-client binary spawning shells or LOLBin script interpreters, which is the only on-endpoint signal an attacker leaves when abusing the platform. Rationale: Article describes the SimpleHelp Technician role as 'remoting into managed endpoints, executing scripts, and more' — the only on-endpoint footprint of that abuse is the customer-client binary spawning shells. Binary name 'Remote Access.exe' (vendor 'SimpleHelp LTD') corroborated by Arctic Wolf's prior SimpleHelp campaign write-up — kept generic on installation path because SimpleHelp installs vary per deployment. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/arctic-wolf-observes-campaign-exploiting-simplehelp-rmm-software-for-initial-access/ • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/
ATT&CKT1219 T1059 T1072
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Help-desk technician runs a legitimate cmd/PowerShell command during a support call
  • MSP-pushed scheduled scripts (patch installers, log collectors) launched via SimpleHelp remote session
  • SimpleHelp's built-in 'Tools' menu running diagnostic commands (ipconfig, systeminfo)
  • Endpoint inventory script invoked by IT during fleet audit
  • Vendor-supplied update wrapped as a script and pushed through SimpleHelp
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildCmd has_any ("\\Get-ComputerInfo", "\\ipconfig", "systeminfo", "\\WindowsUpdate")) and not (AccountName in~ ("known-helpdesk-svc"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full child command line, SHA256, and the Technician name driving the SimpleHelp session from server.log within ±2 min of the spawn; check if the Technician is a known-good IdP user. 2) Contain — if the Technician is unknown / brand-new / has a suspicious email domain, kill the SimpleHelp session, isolate the affected endpoint via MDE, disable the Technician account on the SimpleHelp server, and rotate any creds typed during the session. 3) Hunt — pivot on the Technician's identity across server.log for every other endpoint they touched in the last 14d; sweep those endpoints for the same parent→child pattern, plus newly written persistence artifacts (services, Run keys, scheduled tasks) attributed to 'Remote Access.exe'.
let Lookback = 7d;
let Lolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Remote Access.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has_any ("SimpleHelp", "SimpleHelp LTD") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "SimpleHelp"
| where FileName in~ (Lolbins)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 7d;
let Lolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "\\Remote Access.exe" or ActingProcessName =~ "Remote Access.exe"
| where (ActingProcessFileCompany has_any ("SimpleHelp", "SimpleHelp LTD")) or ActingProcessName has "SimpleHelp"
| extend ChildExe = tostring(split(TargetProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where tolower(ChildExe) in (Lolbins)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SimpleHelp Remote Access Spawning Shell or LOLBin Script Interpreter
id: 6a3f1f0a-9b1e-4d2d-8e7f-9c2b8b1f4d22
description: Detects the SimpleHelp customer-client process ('Remote Access.exe', SimpleHelp LTD) spawning shells or LOLBin script interpreters. After CVE-2026-48558, rogue OIDC-registered Technicians can drive arbitrary script execution on managed endpoints via this exact chain.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/simplehelp-bug-lets-hackers-create-rogue-remote-support-accounts/
  - https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/15
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1072
  - attack.execution
  - attack.lateral_movement
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\Remote Access.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate help-desk troubleshooting via SimpleHelp remote session
  - MSP-driven scripted maintenance jobs
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\Remote\ Access.exe OR *\\remote\ access.exe OR *\\REMOTE\ ACCESS.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\RunDll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\RegSvr32.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^remote access\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
| count > 0
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_name) as childExes values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Remote Access.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstSeen >= relative_time(now(),"-7d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_name) as childExes values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Remote Access.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstSeen >= relative_time(now(),"-7d")
Internet-exposed SimpleHelp servers vulnerable to CVE-2026-48558 AIReconnaissance High
Asset-surface hunt for SimpleHelp servers running 5.5.15 or older / 6.0 pre-release that are reachable from the internet — the entire prerequisite for CVE-2026-48558 exploitation. Lets the SOC drive emergency patching to 5.5.16 / 6.0RC2 before opportunistic exploitation. Rationale: Article gives the exact patched versions (5.5.16, 6.0RC2 released June 9 2026) and prerequisite (internet-exposed server with OIDC). Detection joins Defender TVM CveId lookup against DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing so SOC can prioritise the ~14,000-server exposure cited by Horizon3.ai's Shodan analysis. Image [3] in the article also visually confirms a rogue Technician landed on a real server console. Cross-checked against: • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/ • https://cve.threatint.eu/CVE/CVE-2026-48558
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SimpleHelp servers behind reverse-proxy/WAF that Defender marks as IsInternetFacing but are not directly reachable on 443
  • Lab/test SimpleHelp 6.0 pre-release instances that intentionally lag patches
  • DR-replica SimpleHelp servers visible to TVM but powered off / firewall-blocked
  • Servers patched in the last 24h that TVM hasn't yet re-scanned
Suppression filter
| where IsInternetFacing == true
Response runbook
1) Triage — for each hit, confirm the SimpleHelp version via the server's About page or `/configuration/version`, validate OIDC is enabled, and identify which Technician Groups have 'Allow group authenticated logins' set. 2) Contain — if internet-facing and unpatched, immediately apply 5.5.16 (5.x branch) or 6.0RC2, and as a stop-gap put an IP allowlist on Technician logins per SimpleHelp's mitigation guidance; rotate any technician API tokens. 3) Hunt — pull /opt/SimpleHelp/logs/server.log on each exposed host for any Technician created since 2026-06-01 with an unknown email domain, and run UC1 retroactively for the last 30 days.
let Vulnerable = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where CveId == "CVE-2026-48558"
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId;
let Exposed = DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId;
Vulnerable
| join kind=leftouter Exposed on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion,
          CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, Timestamp desc
let Vulnerable = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where CveId == "CVE-2026-48558"
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId;
let Exposed = DeviceInfo
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId;
Vulnerable
| join kind=leftouter Exposed on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion,
          CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, TimeGenerated desc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Vulnerabilities.severity) as severity values(Vulnerabilities.signature) as signature values(Vulnerabilities.vendor_product) as product from datamodel=Vulnerabilities where (Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-48558" OR (Vulnerabilities.vendor_product="SimpleHelp" AND Vulnerabilities.signature="SimpleHelp" AND Vulnerabilities.severity="critical")) by Vulnerabilities.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Vulnerabilities.severity) as severity values(Vulnerabilities.signature) as signature values(Vulnerabilities.vendor_product) as product from datamodel=Vulnerabilities where (Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-48558" OR (Vulnerabilities.vendor_product="SimpleHelp" AND Vulnerabilities.signature="SimpleHelp" AND Vulnerabilities.severity="critical")) by Vulnerabilities.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
Newly created SimpleHelp Technician immediately exercises privileged actions AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates a brand-new Technician registration in SimpleHelp server.log with privileged actions (remote-session start, script execution, group/role change) by that same account within minutes. The compressed timeline is the signature of CVE-2026-48558 abuse — legitimate onboarding flows have a HR/training gap. Rationale: Article emphasises that the rogue Technician is *immediately* usable for 'remoting into managed endpoints, executing scripts'. Kill-chain block phase 4 detection hint: 'Newly created Technician accounts immediately exercising privileged actions ... shortly after first login'. The 15-minute window keeps onboarding-with-immediate-use FPs but eliminates legitimate flows where HR creates the account hours before first use. Cross-checked against: • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/disclosures/cve-2026-48558-simplehelp-authentication-bypass-iocs/
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1098 T1219
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MSP runbook that provisions a Technician and immediately runs a smoke-test remote session
  • Migration scripts during the 5.5.16 / 6.0RC2 upgrade that re-create Technicians and validate access
  • Just-in-time access tooling that creates an ephemeral Technician for a single ticket
  • QA engineer creating a Technician and self-testing within minutes
Suppression filter
| where DelaySec >= 5
Response runbook
1) Triage — capture the new Technician's username, email, OIDC sub claim, source IP, and the exact privileged action taken (which managed endpoint did they hit, which script ran). 2) Contain — disable the Technician account in SimpleHelp, kill any in-flight remote sessions to the targeted endpoints, isolate those endpoints via MDE, and snapshot for forensics; if the server is still on a vulnerable version, patch to 5.5.16 / 6.0RC2 immediately. 3) Hunt — for the source IP and OIDC sub claim, enumerate all SimpleHelp authentications and every endpoint the rogue Technician interacted with; on each endpoint, run UC2 retro-active and inspect created services, scheduled tasks, and outbound C2 connections from 'Remote Access.exe' or its children.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 15m;
let Creations = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName has "SimpleHelp" or SyslogMessage has "SimpleHelp"
    | where SyslogMessage matches regex @"(?i)technician.*?(created|registered|added)"
    | extend NewUser = extract(@"(?i)technician[^\w]+([\w._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | where isnotempty(NewUser)
    | project CreateTime = TimeGenerated, NewUser, Computer, CreationMsg = SyslogMessage;
let PrivActions = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName has "SimpleHelp" or SyslogMessage has "SimpleHelp"
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("remote session", "script", "group modified", "configuration changed", "role", "privilege")
    | extend ActorUser = extract(@"(?i)(?:user|technician|by)[^\w]+([\w._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | where isnotempty(ActorUser)
    | project ActionTime = TimeGenerated, ActorUser, Computer, ActionMsg = SyslogMessage;
Creations
| join kind=inner (PrivActions) on $left.NewUser == $right.ActorUser
| where ActionTime between (CreateTime .. CreateTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ActionTime, CreateTime)
| project CreateTime, ActionTime, DelaySec, NewUser, Computer, CreationMsg, ActionMsg
| order by ActionTime desc

Vitest Browser API listening on all interfaces (CVE-2026-53633 pre-condition) AIWeaponization High
Hunts for Vitest Browser Mode launched with browser.api.host=0.0.0.0, which exposes the CDP-capable WebSocket RPC to the network. Per CVE-2026-53633, this is the deploy-time misconfiguration that turns the local-only CDP bridge into a remotely exploitable RCE pre-condition, even when allowWrite/allowExec are false. Rationale: Pivots on the exact flag combo named in the article repro (`api: { host: '0.0.0.0' }`) plus the vitest/@vitest/browser/vite-plus package names from the GHSA affected-packages list. Article explicitly identifies this as the network-exposure precondition.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit developer intentionally exposing Vitest to a teammate over LAN for pair-debugging
  • CI runners that bind Vitest to 0.0.0.0 inside a container by design
  • Docker-compose dev stacks where 0.0.0.0 is required for port-forwarding to host
  • E2E test rigs that deliberately expose the browser API to a remote orchestrator
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("build-","ci-","runner-") and AccountName has_any ("ci","build","jenkins","github-actions"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the host is a developer/CI workstation and identify whether the bind to 0.0.0.0 was intentional. Check ProcessCommandLine for whether allowWrite/allowExec are also present and what their values are. Capture the parent process and the package.json scripts that launched node. Step 2 (contain): If unintentional, kill the node.exe PID and block inbound 63315 (or the discovered Vitest port) at the host firewall. If intentional, scope exposure: is the dev machine reachable from VPN/internet? Step 3 (hunt): Search DeviceNetworkEvents for any non-loopback inbound connections to that PID's listening port during its lifetime, and pivot on DeviceFileEvents for writes to vite.config.* or vitest.config.* by browser processes on the same host within the same session.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "node.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "browser.api.host" and ProcessCommandLine has "0.0.0.0"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where CommandLine has "browser.api.host" and CommandLine has "0.0.0.0"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Vitest Browser API Listening on All Interfaces (CVE-2026-53633)
id: 7c1a9f4e-2b3a-4d2c-9e0e-9b1d8c4f1e23
description: Detects node.exe launched as Vitest Browser Mode with browser.api.host=0.0.0.0, exposing the CDP-capable WebSocket RPC to the network and creating the pre-condition for CVE-2026-53633 RCE.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-85jm-7xhm
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\node.exe'
  selection_cmd_vitest:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'vitest'
      - '@vitest/browser'
      - 'vite-plus'
  selection_cmd_host:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'browser.api.host'
      - '0.0.0.0'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd_vitest and selection_cmd_host
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) (@CommandLine:*vitest* OR @CommandLine:*"@vitest/browser"* OR @CommandLine:*vite-plus*) @CommandLine:*browser.api.host* @CommandLine:*0.0.0.0*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(vitest|@vitest\/browser|vite-plus)/i
| CommandLine=/browser\.api\.host/i
| CommandLine=/0\.0\.0\.0/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="node.exe" Processes.process="*vitest*" Processes.process="*browser.api.host*" Processes.process="*0.0.0.0*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="node.exe" Processes.process="*vitest*" Processes.process="*browser.api.host*" Processes.process="*0.0.0.0*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Inbound non-loopback connection to Vitest browser API listener (TCP/63315) AIDelivery High
Detects external/non-loopback inbound connections accepted by node.exe on TCP/63315, the default Vitest browser API port per the article. Reaching the listener is a prerequisite for the CDP-via-WebSocket exploit chain in CVE-2026-53633. Rationale: 63315 is the literal port shown in the article's repro (`http://localhost:63315`). Combining listener-side process identity (node.exe running vitest) with non-loopback remote source is the article-specific signal — generic 'port 63315 open' alone would be noisier.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer pair-programming where a teammate hits the colleague's dev server over LAN
  • Container-to-container traffic inside a docker-compose dev environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Nessus/Qualys) probing the high port
  • E2E test orchestrators in CI connecting to the spawned Vitest browser API
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteIP startswith "10." or RemoteIP startswith "192.168." or RemoteIP startswith "172.16." or RemoteIP startswith "172.17." or RemoteIP startswith "172.18.")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the remote IP, geolocate, and check whether it's a known dev/CI peer or external. Pull DeviceProcessEvents for the receiving node.exe to confirm Vitest Browser Mode and whether host=0.0.0.0 was set. Step 2 (contain): Block 63315 inbound at the host firewall, kill the node.exe listener, and rotate any source-controlled secrets that the project root may contain. Step 3 (hunt): Within the connection window, look for DeviceFileEvents writing `vite.config.*` / `vitest.config.*` files initiated by a browser binary (chrome/chromium/msedge/headless_shell), and pivot on DeviceProcessEvents for any node.exe child shell/LOLBin spawned in the next 60 seconds — those are the post-exploitation signals.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ListeningConnectionCreated","ConnectionAccepted")
| where LocalPort == 63315
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where RemoteIPType != "Loopback" and RemoteIP !startswith "169.254"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemoteIPType, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstPortNumber == 63315
| where NetworkDirection =~ "Inbound"
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr) and SrcIpAddr !startswith "127." and SrcIpAddr != "::1" and not(ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcPortNumber, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Inbound Connection to Vitest Browser API Port 63315 (CVE-2026-53633)

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src_ips from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port=63315 All_Traffic.transport=tcp by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | iplocation src_ips | where NOT cidrmatch("127.0.0.0/8", src_ips) AND NOT cidrmatch("::1/128", src_ips)
Vitest false-sense-of-security config: allowWrite/allowExec false but CDP bridge exposed AIWeaponization High
Detects the precise dangerous configuration the CVE-2026-53633 advisory calls out: Vitest started with allowWrite:false and allowExec:false (operator believes it is safe) while host is bound externally, exposing the CDP RPC that bypasses both flags. Higher-fidelity than the bare 0.0.0.0 hunt because it captures intent + the gap. Rationale: Targets the literal misconfiguration the advisory names: 'In a verified reproduction with allowWrite: false and allowExec: false, CDP Page.setDownloadBehavior set the browser download directory...'. Three-flag combo (host=0.0.0.0 + allowWrite=false + allowExec=false) is rarer than any single flag and reads as 'thought-they-were-safe operator'.
ATT&CKT1190 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit dev who copy-pasted the GHSA reproduction config verbatim to verify their own exposure
  • Security researcher running a local PoC for the CVE
  • Teams who set the flags as a hardening attempt without realising the CDP gap
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the user is a developer and ask whether they intentionally exposed the API while disabling write/exec — explain the CDP bypass and link the GHSA. Step 2 (contain): Have them either upgrade @vitest/browser past the patched version (>5.0.0-beta.3, fix on the 4.x/3.x lines per advisory) OR bind to 127.0.0.1 instead of 0.0.0.0. Step 3 (hunt): On the same host within the listener's lifetime, search DeviceNetworkEvents for non-loopback inbound to the discovered port and DeviceFileEvents for `vite.config.*` writes by a browser binary — those would indicate the misconfiguration was actually weaponised.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "node.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowWrite\s*[:=]\s*false"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowExec\s*[:=]\s*false"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "browser.api.host" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("0.0.0.0","::")
| where not(ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowCDP\s*[:=]\s*false")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite-plus")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowWrite\s*[:=]\s*false"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowExec\s*[:=]\s*false"
| where CommandLine has "browser.api.host" and (CommandLine has "0.0.0.0" or CommandLine has "::")
| where not(CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)allowCDP\s*[:=]\s*false")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

vite/vitest config file modified by browser-context process (CVE-2026-53633 payload drop) AIInstallation High
Detects creation or modification of vite.config.* or vitest.config.* files where the writing process is a browser binary (chromium/chrome/msedge/headless_shell/firefox/playwright). This is the verified impact described in the advisory — CDP Page.setDownloadBehavior + Runtime.evaluate causes the browser to 'download' a malicious vite.config.ts into the project root, which Vitest then reloads and executes. Rationale: Uses the exact file targeted in the advisory repro (`vite.config.ts`, written via `<a download="vite.config.ts">`) plus the CDP-capable browser binaries the advisory names (Playwright Chromium). A browser writing a build-system config file in a project root is anomalous regardless of CVE — and for this specific vector it's the smoking gun.
ATT&CKT1546 T1059.007 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using a browser-based 'Save As' to manually overwrite their own config (rare and observable)
  • Web IDE / StackBlitz-style PWAs writing project files via the File System Access API
  • Browser extensions like 'Save All Resources' grabbing dev assets that happen to be named vite.config.ts
  • Visual config-editor UIs that emit a downloaded config (treat as policy violation)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Diff the new vite.config.* against version control (git log/blame on the file). Any non-developer-authored changes — process.spawn, child_process, http imports, eval, dynamic require — confirm the exploit. Capture file SHA256, FileOriginUrl, and the InitiatingProcessCommandLine to recover the spawning Playwright/Chromium invocation. Step 2 (contain): Kill the Vitest node.exe parent immediately (config-reload hasn't necessarily fired yet); revert the config from git; block 63315 inbound at the host firewall; rotate any secrets the project root exposed (npm tokens, .env files, AWS creds, SSH keys). Step 3 (hunt): Within the next 60 seconds of the file write, look for node.exe spawning shells / LOLBins (cmd, powershell, sh, bash, curl, wget, certutil) and for outbound network from node.exe to non-corp destinations — those indicate the config-reload-to-RCE step fired.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)^(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|cjs)$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("chrome.exe","chromium.exe","msedge.exe","msedgewebview2.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","headless_shell.exe","playwright.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, PreviousFileName, PreviousFolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileOriginUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|cjs)$"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","chromium.exe","msedge.exe","msedgewebview2.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","headless_shell.exe","playwright.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WebSocket access to Vitest browser API tester endpoint (CVE-2026-53633 exploit signature) AIExploitation High
Hunts proxy/WAF/IDS records for HTTP-upgrade or HTTP requests targeting `/__vitest_browser_api__?type=tester` or the `/__vitest_test__/` runner page on port 63315. The advisory's step 3 shows the literal URI used to authenticate to the CDP RPC bridge as a tester client, which is the active-exploit signature. Rationale: Pivots on the literal URI path `/__vitest_browser_api__?type=tester` and the runner page `/__vitest_test__/` quoted verbatim in the advisory's repro steps 1 and 3, plus the `sendCdpEvent` RPC method name from step 4. These strings will not appear in legitimate traffic.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vitest's own browser session connecting to its own API (loopback only — filter)
  • Internal CI runners visiting the Vitest UI for debugging via the official `?type=client` (not `tester`) flow
  • Documentation pages on the Vitest site referencing the path strings (in user-agent of a researcher's browser)
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !startswith "127." and SourceIP != "::1"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify SourceIP — was the access from loopback (legit Vitest internal) or a remote IP? Pull the full URL chain to extract sessionId, projectName, projectName and confirm the format matches the advisory's tester URL shape. Step 2 (contain): If remote, block source IP at perimeter, force-kill the receiving Vitest node.exe, and treat the workstation as compromised pending DFIR. Rotate any project-root secrets and the npm/pnpm tokens cached on the host. Step 3 (hunt): Within the same connection window, hunt for `vite.config.*` writes by a browser process on the destination host (UC4), node.exe spawning child shells (UC6), and additional CDP method names in payloads (`Page.setDownloadBehavior`, `Runtime.evaluate`) via deep packet inspection or Zeek `ws.message` records.
DeviceNetworkEvents

| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("__vitest_browser_api__","__vitest_test__")

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc

Config-reload RCE: node.exe spawns shell/LOLBin within 30s of vite/vitest config write AIExploitation High
Temporal correlation that catches the CVE-2026-53633 RCE moment: vite.config.* is overwritten, Vitest's HMR reloads the new config, and the Node.js payload spawns cmd/powershell/bash/curl/etc. The short window (≤30s) plus the node parent disambiguates legitimate dev-script execution from exploit-triggered execution. Rationale: Models the article's verified RCE chain explicitly: 'vite.config.ts is overwritten with attacker-controlled content. Vitest reloads the changed config. The injected Node.js payload runs on the host.' Constrains parent node.exe to a Vitest invocation (rules out generic npm-script shell spawns) and bounds the delta to 30s (the HMR reload window) to keep precision high.
ATT&CKT1546 T1059 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually editing vite.config in an editor and triggering an npm script that legitimately spawns a shell as part of hot-reload
  • Vitest's own postinstall / test-setup scripts that shell out (e.g. running a docker-compose up via execa)
  • HMR config reload triggering a legitimate `child_process.spawn` in a project that intentionally calls out (rare; review per project)
  • Webpack/Vite plugins that spawn helper processes (graphql codegen, prisma generate) on config change
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildCmd has_any ("prisma generate","graphql-codegen","docker-compose","esbuild","tsc --build","husky install") and ConfigWriter !in~ ("chrome.exe","chromium.exe","msedge.exe","msedgewebview2.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","headless_shell.exe","playwright.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the ChildCmd and NodeCmd from the alert. If ChildCmd is a known build helper (codegen, docker, prisma) chained off an explicit script in package.json, demote. If ChildCmd is a download (curl/wget/certutil/bitsadmin) or contains base64/encoded payloads, treat as confirmed RCE. Diff the new vite.config.* against git to recover the injected payload. Step 2 (contain): Kill the node.exe process tree, isolate the host (network containment / EDR isolate), and revert the config from git. Rotate every credential the developer's session could have touched: SSH keys, AWS keys, GitHub PATs, npm tokens, browser-stored cookies. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot DeviceNetworkEvents off the child PID for C2 callbacks; search the entire dev-team device fleet for any vite.config.* write by a browser binary (UC4) and any inbound to 63315 (UC2) in the past 30 days; check the same dev's commit history for accidental commit of the poisoned config.
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let ConfigWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)^(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|cjs)$"
    | project ConfigWriteTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ConfigPath = FolderPath, ConfigFile = FileName, ConfigWriter = InitiatingProcessFileName, WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
ConfigWrites
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite")
    | where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wmic.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","net.exe","netsh.exe")
    | project ChildSpawnTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ChildProcess = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, NodeCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, NodeFolderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
) on DeviceId
| where ChildSpawnTime between (ConfigWriteTime .. ConfigWriteTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ChildSpawnTime, ConfigWriteTime)
| project ConfigWriteTime, ChildSpawnTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, AccountName, ConfigPath, ConfigFile, ConfigWriter, WriterCmd, ChildProcess, ChildCmd, NodeCmd
| order by ConfigWriteTime desc
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let ConfigWrites = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(vite|vitest)\.config\.(ts|js|mjs|cjs)$"
    | project ConfigWriteTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ConfigPath = TargetFilePath, ConfigFile = TargetFileName, ConfigWriter = ActingProcessName;
ConfigWrites
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ParentProcessName has "node.exe"
    | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("vitest","@vitest/browser","vite")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wmic.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
    | project ChildSpawnTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ChildProcess = ActingProcessName, ChildCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, NodeCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
) on DvcHostname
| where ChildSpawnTime between (ConfigWriteTime .. ConfigWriteTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ChildSpawnTime, ConfigWriteTime)
| project ConfigWriteTime, ChildSpawnTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ConfigPath, ConfigFile, ConfigWriter, ChildProcess, ChildCmd, NodeCmd
| order by ConfigWriteTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) @ParentCommandLine:*vitest* @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\bash.exe OR *\\sh.exe OR *\\wmic.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/node\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|bash|sh|wmic|curl|wget|bitsadmin|certutil|rundll32|regsvr32)\.exe$/i

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/

    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'

level: high

Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails

The Hacker News
2026-06-15 13 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email. The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message
