Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] INFINITERED Trojanized REDCap System File on Disk (SHA256) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound Connection to UNC6508 C2 Infrastructure (23.169.65.49) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] UNC6508 Google Workspace Domain Content Compliance Rule with External BCC · [LLM] UNC6508 Content Compliance Rule with Espionage Keywords (Patroit / chikungunya) · [LLM] Gmail User-Level Forwarding/Filter Rule to External Address · [LLM] Gmail Mailbox Delegation Granted to External Principal · [LLM] Admin/Service Account Mailbox Fan-Out (Mass Mailbox Access in Short Window) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
UNC6508 Google Workspace Domain Content Compliance Rule with External BCC AIActions on Objectives High
Detects creation/modification of Google Workspace domain-level content compliance rules that silently BCC matching messages to an external (Gmail) address. UNC6508 used exactly this admin feature for stealth exfiltration without dropping malware on the mail tier. Rationale: GTIG report explicitly names domain content compliance rules with BCC to a Gmail address as UNC6508's exfiltration vector. The detection keys on admin operation + content_compliance subject + BCC/forward verb + external-domain destination — every component is article-supplied. Cross-checked against MITRE T1098.002 / T1114.003 and existing Sigma rules (no overlap for the GSuite content_compliance + BCC combo). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/003/ • https://services.google.com/fh/files/blogs/google-threat-intel-defense-sector-report.pdf
ATT&CKT1098.002 T1114.003 T1556
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes Authentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate compliance program BCCing to a corporate journaling mailbox (often on a different domain)
  • DLP rule that quarantines outbound mail to a legal-hold archive address
  • Migration tooling creating temporary forward-to-Gmail rules during a tenant cutover
  • Approved e-discovery vendor adding a journal rule to its own collection mailbox
  • MSP/MSSP onboarding scripts standing up compliance copies for monitoring
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountDisplayName has_any ("compliance@","legal@","ediscovery@","journal@") and RawText has_any ("proofpoint.com","mimecast.com","barracuda.com","global-relay.com"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the rule via Admin SDK and verify the destination address, keyword list, and creating admin. Compare the source IP/UserAgent of the admin action against that admin's normal sign-in pattern in SigninLogs/AADSignInEventsBeta. Step 2 (contain): Disable the rule (do not delete — preserve for forensics), revoke active sessions for the creating admin account, force password reset + step-up MFA, and check for any sibling rules created in the same window. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the creating admin's recent activity for new OAuth grants, app passwords, super-admin role assignments; review the keyword list against your sensitive-data taxonomy; pull all mail audit log entries showing BCC delivery to the destination address since rule creation and notify legal/IR.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application has_cs "Google"
| where IsAdminOperation == true
| where ActionType has_any ("CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING","CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING","Create rule","Update rule","compliance","CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING","CHANGE_APPLICATION_SETTING")
| extend RawText = tostring(RawEventData)
| where RawText has_any ("content_compliance","CONTENT_COMPLIANCE","content compliance","contentCompliance")
| where RawText has_any ("BCC","Bcc","bcc","forward","copyMessage")
| where RawText has "gmail.com" or RawText matches regex @"@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, ObjectName, RawText
let ExternalDomainPattern = @"@(?!yourorg\.com$)[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}";
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GSuite","GoogleWorkspace","Workspace")
| where Operation has_any ("CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING","CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING","CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING","create_rule","content_compliance")
| extend Raw = tostring(EventData)
| where Raw has_any ("content_compliance","contentCompliance","CONTENT_COMPLIANCE")
| where Raw has_any ("BCC","Bcc","bcc","forward","copyMessage")
| where Raw matches regex ExternalDomainPattern
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, UserAgent, Operation, ObjectId, Raw

UNC6508 Content Compliance Rule with Espionage Keywords (Patroit / chikungunya) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects creation of GWS content compliance / forwarding rules whose keyword list overlaps UNC6508's published collection priorities — the misspelled 'Patroit' tag, 'chikungunya' (highly specific to the 2025 Guangdong outbreak the actor watched), uncrewed vehicles, and offensive-cyber terminology. Rationale: Article gives a highly specific keyword the actor used ('Patroit' — note the misspelling) plus 'chikungunya' (linked to the 2025 Guangdong outbreak the actor was watching). These two strings alone are near-zero-FP in legitimate compliance rules. Adds CUI/FOUO/ITAR as defense-research analogues per article's collection-priority list. Cross-checked against: • https://services.google.com/fh/files/blogs/google-threat-intel-defense-sector-report.pdf • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/003/
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1213
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red team simulating UNC6508 with the same keyword list
  • Threat-intel team setting up canary rules using published IOCs
  • Research librarian creating an alerting rule for a literature watch on chikungunya (medical research orgs only)
  • Compliance team building a CUI/FOUO data-loss rule that legitimately uses those terms
  • DLP policy migration that imports a published keyword pack
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountDisplayName has "redteam" or AccountDisplayName has "purple-team" or RawText has "canary")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full rule definition (keyword list + destination). If 'Patroit' or 'chikungunya' appear, treat as TP until proven otherwise — these are signature of UNC6508. Verify creating admin's last 30 days of activity. Step 2 (contain): Disable the rule but preserve definition, revoke admin sessions, rotate admin credentials, enforce phishing-resistant MFA on all super-admins, and audit Workspace super-admin role assignments since September 2023 (earliest known UNC6508 dwell). Step 3 (hunt): Search 90 days of mail audit logs for BCC delivery to any address in the destination list; pivot on any REDCap-hosting servers in the org for INFINITERED hashes; engage Google Workspace security and GTIG for IOC enrichment.

title: UNC6508 GWS Compliance Rule with Espionage-Specific Keywords
id: 8f4b1d92-3c5e-4a76-b29d-7e6f1c4a8b22
description: Detects Google Workspace compliance/forwarding rule creation containing UNC6508-attributed keywords including the misspelled tag 'Patroit', 'chikungunya', and CUI/FOUO terms.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/chinese-hackers-abused-google-workspace.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1114.003
logsource:
  product: gsuite
  service: admin
detection:
  selection:
    eventName:
      - 'CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING'
      - 'CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING'
      - 'CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING'
      - 'CHANGE_APPLICATION_SETTING'
  keywords:
    EventData|contains:
      - 'Patroit'
      - 'chikungunya'
      - 'Guangdong'
      - 'uncrewed'
      - 'offensive cyber'
      - 'FOUO'
      - 'CUI'
      - 'ITAR'
  condition: selection and keywords
level: critical
source:gsuite @evt.name:(CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING OR CHANGE_GMAIL_SETTING OR CREATE_APPLICATION_SETTING) (@event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*Patroit* OR @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*chikungunya* OR @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*Guangdong* OR @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*uncrewed* OR @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*"offensive cyber"* OR @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*FOUO* OR @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*CUI* OR @event.parameters.NEW_VALUE:*ITAR*)
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object_path) as object_path values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | search object_path="*Patroit*" OR object_path="*chikungunya*" OR object_path="*Guangdong*" OR object_path="*uncrewed*" OR object_path="*offensive cyber*" OR object_path="*FOUO*" OR object_path="*CUI*" OR object_path="*ITAR*" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object_path) as object_path values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | search object_path="*Patroit*" OR object_path="*chikungunya*" OR object_path="*Guangdong*" OR object_path="*uncrewed*" OR object_path="*offensive cyber*" OR object_path="*FOUO*" OR object_path="*CUI*" OR object_path="*ITAR*" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Outbound Connection to UNC6508 C2 Infrastructure (23.169.65.49) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects any host-side connection to 23.169.65.49 — the UNC6508 C2 IP that INFINITERED uses for HTTP-cookie command tasking. Article-provided IOC; high-confidence on any inbound or outbound hit. Rationale: 23.169.65.49 is the only IP indicator the article provides for UNC6508 / INFINITERED C2. Direct IOC match, no derivation needed. Cross-referenced MITRE for T1071.001 + T1102 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / sandbox sandbox host detonating the IOC for analysis
  • Threat-intel feed ingestion box that resolves indicators to enrich
  • NAT/proxy egress shared with other tenants where the IP is reused by a benign service later
  • Red-team purple exercise replaying the IOC
  • Internet-wide scanner traffic (rare for outbound but possible for inbound)
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","malware-lab","ti-enrich"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm direction (inbound to a REDCap server vs outbound from a workstation — the article describes both shapes). Pull the initiating process, account, and parent. For inbound, capture the HTTP cookie value if proxy/WAF logs are available. Step 2 (contain): Block 23.169.65.49 at perimeter + EDR network containment for hits; isolate the host pending IR triage. Step 3 (hunt): Hash-match the seven INFINITERED SHA256s on the host's filesystem; pivot REDCap install path for trojanized system files; review domain admin authentication trail for the dwell window (Sept 2023 onward); audit GWS content compliance rules per UC #1.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteIP == "23.169.65.49" or LocalIP == "23.169.65.49"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, Protocol, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where DestinationIP == "23.169.65.49" or SourceIP == "23.169.65.49"
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourcePort, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where DstIpAddr == "23.169.65.49" or SrcIpAddr == "23.169.65.49"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where RemoteIp == "23.169.65.49"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType)

INFINITERED Trojanized REDCap System File on Disk (SHA256) AIInstallation Medium
Hash-matches the seven INFINITERED SHA256s GTIG published. Catches trojanized REDCap PHP/system files dropped during the install hijack stage, including persistence across upgrades. Rationale: Direct hash IOC from the article (all seven INFINITERED SHA256s pre-extracted). Hash matches are the highest-fidelity signal possible — single-source FP probability ~zero. Falcon LogScale query targets FileWritten because REDCap servers are typically Linux PHP, where INFINITERED trojanizes system files on disk before execution. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1554/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1554 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel team uploading the hash to a malware sandbox for analysis
  • Security tool downloading the IOC list locally for offline scanning
  • Lab/sandbox detonation of the published IOCs
  • Incident-response analyst staging samples for reverse engineering
  • Backup system replicating quarantined files between sandbox hosts
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","malware-lab","ti-research") or FolderPath has_any ("\\quarantine\\","\\samples\\","/quarantine/","/samples/"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify whether the host is a production REDCap server. If so, treat as confirmed compromise — INFINITERED reinjects on upgrade, so 'newest version' is not safe. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, snapshot disk + memory, kill the web service, block any C2 IPs at perimeter, and preserve the trojanized files for IR. Do NOT just reinstall REDCap — article notes the upgrade-hijack persistence. Step 3 (hunt): Search all internet-facing REDCap servers for the same hashes; review server access logs for the dwell window (back to Sept 2023); audit local DB tables for stolen credential dumps stored by INFINITERED; rotate every credential ever used to log into the affected REDCap instances; pivot to GWS audit logs per UCs #1/#2.
let INFINITERED_HASHES = dynamic(["ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7","db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136","c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b","8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec","51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045","4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b","58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
  | where SHA256 in (INFINITERED_HASHES)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
  | where SHA256 in (INFINITERED_HASHES) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (INFINITERED_HASHES)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName)
let INFINITERED_HASHES = dynamic(["ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7","db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136","c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b","8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec","51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045","4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b","58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
  | where TargetFileSHA256 in (INFINITERED_HASHES)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
  | where FileHash in (INFINITERED_HASHES)
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceHostName, FilePath, FileHash, SourceUserName)

Gmail User-Level Forwarding/Filter Rule to External Address AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects creation of per-user Gmail forwarding or filter-with-forward rules whose destination is outside the org's primary domain — the user-tier analog of the domain content compliance rule UNC6508 abused, and a common companion persistence mechanism if domain-level rules get detected and removed. Rationale: Article reviewer flagged that GWS 'rules' includes user-level forwarding/filters as a sibling persistence path; article explicitly recommends auditing 'mail-forwarding rules' alongside content compliance. External-domain extraction with org-domain anti-filter is the standard high-fidelity shape. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/003/ • https://support.google.com/a/answer/9300435
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1098.002
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User legitimately forwarding work mail to a personal/recovery account during PTO
  • Approved partner integration that forwards mail to a vendor inbox
  • Departing employee setting an external out-of-office forward
  • Test/QA account configured to forward to an external test inbox
  • User signing up for a third-party SaaS that requires email forwarding for ticketing
Suppression filter
| where not (FwdDomain in ("gmail.com","outlook.com","yahoo.com") and AccountDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)test|qa|sandbox")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm whether the forward destination is on an approved list or the user's own recovery address (admin SDK lookup). Compare creation IP/UserAgent to user baseline. Step 2 (contain): If suspicious, disable the rule, revoke active sessions, force MFA re-enrollment, and notify the user. Step 3 (hunt): Search sibling accounts in the same team/department for new external forwards (UNC6508 created bulk rules); pivot to AAD/Workspace sign-ins for the user across the prior 90 days; check for delegation grants (UC #6) created by the same admin.
let CorporateDomains = dynamic(["yourorg.com","yourorg.org"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application has_cs "Google"
| where ActionType has_any ("email_forwarding_out_of_domain","Create Filter","Email forwarding","FORWARDING_RULE","CHANGE_USER_SETTING")
| extend RawText = tostring(RawEventData)
| where RawText has_any ("forward","forwardingAddress","FORWARD")
| extend FwdDomain = tolower(extract(@"forward[^@]{0,40}@([A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, RawText))
| where isnotempty(FwdDomain)
| where not(FwdDomain in (CorporateDomains))
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, ObjectName, FwdDomain, RawText
let CorporateDomains = dynamic(["yourorg.com","yourorg.org"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GSuite","GoogleWorkspace","Workspace")
| where Operation has_any ("CREATE_FILTER","email_forwarding_out_of_domain","CHANGE_USER_SETTING","FORWARDING_RULE")
| extend Raw = tostring(EventData)
| where Raw has_any ("forward","forwardingAddress","FORWARD")
| extend FwdDomain = tolower(extract(@"forward[^@]{0,40}@([A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, Raw))
| where isnotempty(FwdDomain) and not(FwdDomain in (CorporateDomains))
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, UserAgent, Operation, ObjectId, FwdDomain, Raw
title: Gmail User-Level Forwarding Rule to External Domain
id: 9a8b1c34-6d2f-4e58-9c47-5f1e2a8b3c66
description: Detects per-user Gmail forwarding or filter-forward rule creation pointing to an address outside the organization's owned domains.

author: SOC Detection Engineering

  - attack.t1098.002

    eventName:
      - 'CREATE_FILTER'
      - 'CHANGE_USER_SETTING'
      - 'email_forwarding_out_of_domain'

    EventData|contains:
      - 'forward'
      - 'forwardingAddress'
  condition: selection and forward
level: medium

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object_path) as object_path values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" (All_Changes.action=created OR All_Changes.action=modified) (All_Changes.object_category="filter" OR All_Changes.object_category="forward" OR All_Changes.change_type="USER_SETTINGS") by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | rex field=object_path "forward.{0,40}@(?<forward_domain>[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})" | search forward_domain!="yourorg.com" forward_domain!="yourorg.org" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Gmail Mailbox Delegation Granted to External Principal AIActions on Objectives High
Detects Gmail delegation grants (Mail Delegate / SendAs / SendOnBehalfOf) where the delegate identity is outside the org's primary domain — a stealthier post-compromise persistence path than forwarding because it leaves no rule visible in the source mailbox. Rationale: Reviewer-supplied path; article emphasizes UNC6508 used 'rules' broadly post-admin-compromise to copy mail. Delegation grants are functionally equivalent to forwarding but invisible in the mailbox owner's settings UI, making them a likely follow-on after detection of the BCC rule. External-domain anti-filter is the strongest single signal. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/002/ • https://support.google.com/mail/answer/138350
ATT&CKT1098.002 T1098.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cross-tenant M&A integration where a parent-org admin gets temporary delegation
  • Executive assistant from a contracted EA service granted delegation
  • Approved external counsel given delegation for e-discovery
  • Departing employee handing off to a contractor with an external email
  • Tenant migration tooling that grants temporary delegate access
Suppression filter
| where not (DelegateDomain in ("approved-partner.com","counsel.example"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm whether the delegate address is on an approved external-collaborator allowlist. Check the granting admin/user's recent sign-in history for impossible travel or new IPs. Step 2 (contain): Revoke the delegation, revoke active sessions for grantor + grantee (if grantee is internal-but-compromised), and rotate the grantor's password + MFA. Step 3 (hunt): Search the prior 90 days for additional delegations granted by the same admin or to the same external address; pivot on the external address against your inbound mail-flow logs and any GWS rule activity (UCs #1, #5); review domain-admin role assignment history.
let CorporateDomains = dynamic(["yourorg.com","yourorg.org"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application has_cs "Google"
| where ActionType has_any ("CREATE_DELEGATE","ADD_DELEGATE","DELEGATE_EMAIL","Add mail delegate","mail.delegate")
| extend RawText = tostring(RawEventData)
| extend DelegateAddr = tolower(extract(@"([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, RawText))
| extend DelegateDomain = tostring(split(DelegateAddr, "@")[1])
| where isnotempty(DelegateDomain) and not(DelegateDomain in (CorporateDomains))
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, ObjectName, DelegateAddr, DelegateDomain, RawText
let CorporateDomains = dynamic(["yourorg.com","yourorg.org"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GSuite","GoogleWorkspace","Workspace")
| where Operation has_any ("CREATE_DELEGATE","ADD_DELEGATE","DELEGATE_EMAIL","mail.delegate")
| extend Raw = tostring(EventData)
| extend DelegateAddr = tolower(extract(@"([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, Raw))
| extend DelegateDomain = tostring(split(DelegateAddr, "@")[1])
| where isnotempty(DelegateDomain) and not(DelegateDomain in (CorporateDomains))
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, UserAgent, Operation, ObjectId, DelegateAddr, DelegateDomain, Raw
title: Gmail Mailbox Delegation to External Principal
id: 5b8e2d44-7c91-4f63-a318-9d4f1c6b5a32
description: Detects Google Workspace mail delegation grants whose delegate address is outside the corporate domain set.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/chinese-hackers-abused-google-workspace.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1098.002
logsource:
  product: gsuite
  service: admin
detection:
  selection:
    eventName:
      - 'CREATE_DELEGATE'
      - 'ADD_DELEGATE'
      - 'DELEGATE_EMAIL'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:gsuite @evt.name:(CREATE_DELEGATE OR ADD_DELEGATE OR DELEGATE_EMAIL) -@event.parameters.DELEGATE_EMAIL:*@yourorg.com*
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.object) as object values(All_Changes.object_path) as object_path values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" (All_Changes.change_type="DELEGATE" OR All_Changes.action="CREATE_DELEGATE" OR All_Changes.action="ADD_DELEGATE") by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | rex field=object_path "delegate.{0,40}@(?<delegate_domain>[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})" | search delegate_domain!="yourorg.com" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.object) as object values(All_Changes.object_path) as object_path values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" (All_Changes.change_type="DELEGATE" OR All_Changes.action="CREATE_DELEGATE" OR All_Changes.action="ADD_DELEGATE") by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | rex field=object_path "delegate.{0,40}@(?<delegate_domain>[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})" | search delegate_domain!="yourorg.com" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Admin/Service Account Mailbox Fan-Out (Mass Mailbox Access in Short Window) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects an admin or service account accessing N or more distinct mailboxes within a 1-hour window — the precondition for the bulk rule-creation step UNC6508 performed after gaining domain-admin in Workspace. Rationale: Reviewer-supplied; article explicitly states UNC6508 reached domain admin and then created the BCC rule — necessarily implying mass-mailbox visibility either directly or via the admin SDK. Fan-out threshold of 10 distinct mailboxes/hour for admin/service accounts is a P99 anomaly versus typical break-glass admin workflows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/002/
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1530 T1114.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate e-discovery search across many custodian mailboxes
  • Org-wide migration tooling enumerating mailboxes during a tenant move
  • Compliance officer running a litigation hold search
  • Backup/archive vendor's service account performing a full sweep
  • Help-desk admin troubleshooting a delivery issue across a distribution list
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountDisplayName has_any ("ediscovery","backup","migration","compliance") or UAs has_any ("Veritas","Mimecast","Proofpoint","Spanning"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the admin/service account and the mailbox set. Cross-check against scheduled e-discovery / migration / backup activity owners. Step 2 (contain): If unexpected, revoke active sessions + OAuth tokens for the account, suspend or rotate credentials, and require step-up phishing-resistant MFA before re-enabling. Step 3 (hunt): Within the same 1-hour window, look for content compliance rule changes (UC #1), per-user forwarding rule additions (UC #5), and delegation grants (UC #6); if any are present, treat as confirmed UNC6508-shape compromise and escalate to IR.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has_cs "Google"
| where IsAdminOperation == true or AccountType has_any ("admin","service")
| where ActionType has_any ("View Item","Access","Read mailbox","List Messages","GET_MAILBOX","Impersonate")
| summarize DistinctMailboxes = dcount(ObjectId), Mailboxes = make_set(ObjectName, 50), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SrcIPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10), UAs = make_set(UserAgent, 10) by AccountDisplayName, AccountId, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where DistinctMailboxes >= 10
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GSuite","GoogleWorkspace","Workspace")
| where UserType in~ ("Admin","Application","ServicePrincipal") or Operation has_any ("Impersonate","GET_MAILBOX","List Messages","View Item")
| summarize DistinctMailboxes = dcount(ObjectId), Mailboxes = make_set(ObjectId, 50), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SrcIPs = make_set(ClientIP, 10) by UserId, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where DistinctMailboxes >= 10
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:gsuite (@evt.name:(GET_MAILBOX OR "List Messages" OR Impersonate OR "View Item") @user.is_admin:true)
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(All_Changes.object) as distinct_mailboxes min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object) as mailboxes values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" All_Changes.user_category="admin" by All_Changes.user span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | where distinct_mailboxes >= 10 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(All_Changes.object) as distinct_mailboxes min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object) as mailboxes values(All_Changes.src) as src from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="Google Workspace" All_Changes.user_category="admin" by All_Changes.user span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | where distinct_mailboxes >= 10 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or SHA1 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or MD5 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
VS Code / Cursor auto-executing shell via tasks.json runOn:folderOpen (Contagious Interview / UNK_DeadDrop) AIDelivery High
Hunts the cornerstone TTP of UNK_DeadDrop / Contagious Interview: a target clones an attacker-controlled GitHub repo and opens it in VS Code or Cursor, at which point a hidden task (often named 'eslint-check') auto-fires a shell/cmd/cscript command via the runOn:folderOpen feature. Detects Code.exe / cursor.exe parenting curl/wget/cmd/powershell/cscript with download-and-execute strings. Rationale: Targets the exact runOn:folderOpen TTP called out as 'the crucial aspect connecting the campaign to Pyongyang' and corroborated by Abstract Security and OpenSourceMalware blogs (the 'eslint-check' task name is the most-observed disguise). Parent of Code.exe/Cursor.exe spawning a shell with download-execute strings is a tight, low-FP signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/dont-fear-repo-unkdeaddrop-phishing-campaign-targets-developers-steal • https://www.abstract.security/blog/contagious-interview-tracking-the-vs-code-tasks-infection-vector • https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/tasksjacker-blog-post
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually running a build/lint task via VS Code task runner
  • Code Runner / ESLint / Prettier extension executing legitimate tooling
  • DevContainer initialisation invoking shell setup scripts
  • Yeoman / npx scaffolding spawning cscript/wscript on Windows
  • Salt-stack / Ansible playbooks invoked from VS Code terminal
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--extensionDevelopmentPath","--inspect-extensions") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm run lint","npm run build","yarn build","vite build"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full ProcessCommandLine + InitiatingProcessCommandLine and inspect the workspace. Use DeviceFileEvents to find .vscode/tasks.json or .githooks/pre-commit written in the last 24h on the same DeviceId — confirm a 'runOn':'folderOpen' or curl|wget pipeline is present. 2) Contain: isolate the device via Defender Live Response, kill the spawned process tree, and revoke any developer credentials accessible from the workstation (GitHub PAT, AWS keys, npm tokens, browser-stored wallet creds). 3) Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessSHA256 of the spawned shell to find sibling infections, query EmailUrlInfo for github.com/<actor> links in the past 30 days, and search DeviceNetworkEvents for the article's C2 (23.137.105.75:5173) and domain set across the fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("eslint-check","runOn","folderOpen","| sh","| bash","IEX","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","curl -s","wget -q")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("eslint-check","folderOpen","| sh","| bash","IEX","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Windows VBScript loader spawning CMD to install malicious VSIX (UNK_DeadDrop Windows chain) AIInstallation High
Detects the Windows-specific UNK_DeadDrop infection chain: a VBScript dropped by the cloned GitHub repo invokes wscript.exe / cscript.exe → cmd.exe → installs a sideloaded VS Code extension via 'code --install-extension'. The pipeline uploads ZIP files and terminates, so the window is short — alerting on the install-extension transitive parent catches it. Rationale: The article states 'Windows attack chain relies on the VBScript payload to run a CMD file, which then installs the extension'. code.exe --install-extension launched from wscript/cscript/cmd is the rendezvous point regardless of which VSIX name the actor uses next — survives rotation of the IOC filenames. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/dont-fear-repo-unkdeaddrop-phishing-campaign-targets-developers-steal • https://cybersecuritynews.com/north-korea-aligned-hackers-abuse-github-repositories/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1176 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Intune / SCCM extension provisioning scripts pushing approved extensions org-wide
  • Developer scripting bulk extension install in PowerShell on a fresh laptop
  • Dev container post-create.sh installing extensions
  • CI runners (GitHub Actions) installing VS Code Server extensions on selfhosted Windows runners
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Intune","SCCM","DevContainer") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("IntuneManagementExtension.exe","ccmexec.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the .vsix path from CommandLine, then query DeviceFileEvents for that path's SHA256 and origin URL. Cross-check against the article's hashes (e.g. 35813f44..., 4c0d9b80...) and the three Yeeth Security extension names. 2) Contain: uninstall the extension with code --uninstall-extension <id>, isolate the host, and search %APPDATA%\Roaming\Code\User\globalStorage for stolen-wallet drop files. 3) Hunt: pivot on the dropping VBScript SHA256 across the fleet and search DeviceNetworkEvents for the C2 23.137.105.75:5173 from the dev workstation segment.
let VsixInstall = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("code.exe","code-cli.exe","Cursor.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--install-extension"
   or ProcessCommandLine has ".vsix";
VsixInstall
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","Code.exe","Cursor.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GrandParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Child = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\code.exe","\\code-cli.exe","\\Cursor.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("--install-extension",".vsix")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

C2 callback to UNK_DeadDrop infrastructure (23.137.105.75:5173 and named domains) AICommand & Control Medium
Atomic IOC detection for outbound connections to UNK_DeadDrop / Contagious Interview C2 infrastructure named by Proofpoint and the article's IOC bundle. Catches both the Linux/macOS persistent Overlord agent and the short-lived Windows ZIP-upload pipeline. Port 5173 is the article's confirmed C2 port; the domain list covers the staging / phishing landing infrastructure. Rationale: Article explicitly names 23.137.105[.]75:5173 as the data exfil endpoint and the IOC bundle provides the full domain set. Port 5173 is unusual (default Vite dev-server port) and a high-fidelity tell for the Overlord HTTP POST channel. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/dont-fear-repo-unkdeaddrop-phishing-campaign-targets-developers-steal • https://cybersecuritynews.com/north-korea-aligned-hackers-abuse-github-repositories/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher reverse-engineering the campaign in a managed sandbox
  • Threat intel team validating an IOC feed against live traffic
  • Pen-test engagement re-using the same C2 for emulation
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName + AccountName + first-seen Timestamp. Determine whether this is Linux/macOS Overlord (long-lived) or Windows short-burst HTTP POST. 2) Contain: block all three IPs and the domain list at the perimeter, isolate any host that hit 23.137.105.75:5173, and rotate any developer credential reachable from that host. 3) Hunt: from the source host, walk back through DeviceProcessEvents 1h prior for VS Code / Cursor parent of shell, query EmailEvents for the recruitment lure that drove the click, and search EmailUrlInfo for github.com/<actor>/repo links to identify other recipients.
let C2_IPs = dynamic(["23.137.105.75","170.205.29.83","170.205.30.227"]);
let C2_Domains = dynamic(["empowerpharmacy.space","nxlog.tech","ondofinance.tech","valorecuiting.online","migadyn.info","contacttrixauvex.ink","trixauvex.org","pulsynk.org","mailtrixauvex.ink","mailpulsynk.xyz","mailpredicttogether.ink","predicttocareer.space","onoplanoai.ink","trixauvexnet.ink","recruitvex.us","nowurisch.fit","hyperdevpipline.org","nemesistrade.work","ceronet.work","deep-ai-guard.store"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2_IPs)
   or (RemoteIP == "23.137.105.75" and RemotePort == 5173)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (C2_Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2_IPs = dynamic(["23.137.105.75","170.205.29.83","170.205.30.227"]);

  (ImNetworkSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where DstIpAddr in (C2_IPs) or (DstIpAddr == "23.137.105.75" and DstPortNumber == 5173) or DstHostname has_any (C2_Domains)
     | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, NetworkProtocol, Url),
  (ImDnsActivity
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where DnsQuery has_any (C2_Domains)
     | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious VS Code extension marketplace install (ByteBinTools / ToolCraft / OLDev jupyter VSIX) AIInstallation Medium
Atomic detection for the three named malicious VS Code extensions Yeeth Security identified on the official marketplace: ByteBinTools.jupyter-powerdev, ToolCraft.jupyter-powertools, OLDev.markdown-mode-devtools. Detects file writes of the specific .vsix filenames or directory creation under the user extensions folder. Rationale: Article names the exact three .vsix filenames Yeeth Security found on the official VS Code marketplace and lists their hashes in the IOC bundle. File-name + extension-folder-path is unambiguous — any hit is a confirmed compromised developer workstation. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1176 T1505
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst storing the VSIX in a sandbox for reverse engineering
  • Threat intel team distributing the IOC to an isolated detonation host
  • Marketplace mirror service caching the (now-removed) extension
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the .vscode/extensions sub-folder still exists and pull all files for forensic review; capture the JavaScript C2 layer payload. 2) Contain: run `code --uninstall-extension <publisher.id>` on every affected host, isolate the host, and rotate all developer credentials (GitHub PAT, npm, Azure DevOps, AWS, browser-stored wallet seeds). 3) Hunt: pivot on SHA256 across the fleet, search CloudAppEvents / OfficeActivity for SharePoint API access from a non-corp UPN (the extension exfils via Graph+SharePoint), and review M365 audit for new App Registrations consented by the developer.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ (
    "ByteBinTools.jupyter-powerdev-2026.6.8.vsix",
    "ToolCraft.jupyter-powertools-3.21.0.vsix",
    "OLDev.markdown-mode-devtools-2.1.0.vsix")
   or FolderPath has_any (
    @"\.vscode\extensions\bytebintools.jupyter-powerdev",
    @"\.vscode\extensions\toolcraft.jupyter-powertools",
    @"\.vscode\extensions\oldev.markdown-mode-devtools")
   or SHA256 in ("35813f4401d3ad77b618275473a556eb47bfa6f4b7439dd8943b19f81aa7252e",
                 "c935808147f0236c81483d7bbeda4b9d602f3595d5d4057f8115d39e222d1c4b",
                 "4c0d9b802c075be79e9edb52d88f8dd72e6904f5c58267213745818470945c78",
                 "62761f38ed194c59abe15c49f09f0ebc431ac852c965180c9327ed84d3a454fb",
                 "d3ebce2f05fe91a8260e87fd11a6ea17c156703d081b3f91d9bbe5fd6aeedc10")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName in~ (
    "ByteBinTools.jupyter-powerdev-2026.6.8.vsix",

  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1176
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - 'ByteBinTools.jupyter-powerdev-2026.6.8.vsix'
      - 'ToolCraft.jupyter-powertools-3.21.0.vsix'
      - 'OLDev.markdown-mode-devtools-2.1.0.vsix'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.vscode\extensions\bytebintools.jupyter-powerdev'
      - '\.vscode\extensions\toolcraft.jupyter-powertools'
      - '\.vscode\extensions\oldev.markdown-mode-devtools'
  condition: selection_name or selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Security team intentionally cataloguing the malicious VSIX for analysis
level: critical
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*ByteBinTools.jupyter-powerdev-2026.6.8.vsix* OR *ToolCraft.jupyter-powertools-3.21.0.vsix* OR *OLDev.markdown-mode-devtools-2.1.0.vsix* OR *\.vscode\extensions\bytebintools.jupyter-powerdev* OR *\.vscode\extensions\toolcraft.jupyter-powertools* OR *\.vscode\extensions\oldev.markdown-mode-devtools*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/(ByteBinTools\.jupyter-powerdev-2026\.6\.8|ToolCraft\.jupyter-powertools-3\.21\.0|OLDev\.markdown-mode-devtools-2\.1\.0)\.vsix$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\\.vscode\\extensions\\(bytebintools\.jupyter-powerdev|toolcraft\.jupyter-powertools|oldev\.markdown-mode-devtools)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

Git hook auto-execution post-clone (Contagious Interview .githooks/pre-commit) AIDelivery Medium
Detects the newer Contagious Interview TTP of dropping malicious .githooks/pre-commit files into 'coding assessment' repos so that the next git commit (or git clone with core.hooksPath configured) silently launches a script. Hunts for git.exe parenting shell/script interpreters or for file writes to .githooks/pre-commit on developer workstations. Rationale: Article explicitly notes 'use of Git hooks (.githooks/pre-commit) to fire the execution of malicious code when a target clones a coding assessment repository, marking a shift from hiding the malicious code within .vscode/tasks.json or package.json files'. Detecting either the file write or the post-clone hook execution catches the new pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html • https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/tasksjacker-blog-post
ATT&CKT1546 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Devs adopting husky / lefthook / pre-commit framework that ships .githooks/ wrappers
  • Monorepo bootstrap scripts that write pre-commit hooks during setup
  • Internal tooling repos that legitimately use .githooks for linting
  • Renovate / Dependabot PRs touching hook files
Suppression filter
and not (TargetFilePath has_any ("husky","lefthook","node_modules\\pre-commit") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "npm install")
Response runbook
1) Triage: cat the .githooks/pre-commit content; compare against repo defaults (most pre-commit framework wrappers are short, well-known). Pull the cloning user's git history with `git log --diff-filter=A --name-only -- .githooks/`. 2) Contain: if malicious, isolate the developer host and remove the hook (`git config --unset core.hooksPath`). Treat git credentials, SSH keys, and any cached tokens as compromised. 3) Hunt: search EmailEvents for inbound 'coding assessment' / 'code review' lures to the same recipient, query DeviceNetworkEvents for the article's C2 IPs/domains from this host, and look for follow-on Overlord behaviour (osascript password prompt on macOS, persistent connection to 23.137.105.75).
let HookFiles = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has ".githooks"
   and FileName in~ ("pre-commit","post-checkout","post-merge","post-clone")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("git.exe","GitHubDesktop.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("clone","fetch","pull")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let HookExec = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","git-bash.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
   and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pre-commit","post-checkout",".githooks")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","node.exe","python.exe","python3.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine;
HookFiles | union HookExec | order by Timestamp desc
let HookFiles = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has ".githooks"
   and TargetFileName in~ ("pre-commit","post-checkout","post-merge");
let HookExec = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("git.exe","git-bash.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
   and ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (".githooks","pre-commit","post-checkout")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","node.exe","python.exe");
HookFiles | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| union (HookExec | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon ((@EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\.githooks\pre-commit* OR *\.githooks\post-checkout* OR */.githooks/pre-commit*)) OR (@EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\git.exe OR *\bash.exe OR *\sh.exe) @ParentCommandLine:(*\.githooks* OR *pre-commit* OR *post-checkout*) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\python.exe)))
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.githooks[\\/](pre-commit|post-checkout|post-merge)$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(git|bash|sh)\.exe$/i ParentCommandLine=/\.githooks|pre-commit|post-checkout/i ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|cscript|wscript|curl|wget|node|python)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\.githooks\\pre-commit*","*/.githooks/pre-commit*","*\\.githooks\\post-checkout*","*/.githooks/post-checkout*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\.githooks\\pre-commit*","*/.githooks/pre-commit*","*\\.githooks\\post-checkout*","*/.githooks/post-checkout*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
DPRK npm supply-chain install (redeem-onchain-sdk / nicegui / period-newline Axios follow-up) AIDelivery High
Detects installation of the three malicious npm packages OpenSourceMalware identified as the Axios supply-chain follow-up: redeem-onchain-sdk@1.0.7, nicegui@0.1.4, period-newline@0.1.0. Catches npm/yarn/pnpm processes resolving these package names or post-install scripts writing the package directory. Rationale: Article identifies these three specific npm packages as the Axios follow-up payloads. Atomic IOC on package name in npm cmdline or under node_modules path is high-fidelity; the actor's pivot speed (18h to new package) makes early detection critical. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat researcher detonating the package in a sandbox
  • Internal package-mirror cache scan re-touching the tarball
  • Dependency scanner (e.g. socket.dev, Snyk) auditing the package list
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the package.json / package-lock.json of the host's recently-touched repos to confirm the package was declared (not just resolved transitively). Capture the postinstall script. 2) Contain: `npm uninstall <pkg>` on affected hosts, purge from npm cache (`npm cache clean`), block the package versions in any internal mirror (Artifactory, Nexus), isolate the developer host, and rotate npm / GitHub / cloud tokens accessible from it. 3) Hunt: scan all repos for the three package names in package-lock.json and yarn.lock, search EmailEvents for crypto-trading-bot GitHub lures, and check for C2 connections to the article's IP set.
let BadPackages = dynamic(["redeem-onchain-sdk","period-newline","nicegui@0.1.4"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (BadPackages)
| union (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\redeem-onchain-sdk",@"\node_modules\period-newline",@"\node_modules\nicegui")
    | where FileName in~ ("package.json","index.js","postinstall.js")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              FolderPath, FileName, SHA256)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadPackages = dynamic(["redeem-onchain-sdk","period-newline","nicegui@0.1.4"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (BadPackages)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| union (
    ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\node_modules\redeem-onchain-sdk",@"\node_modules\period-newline",@"\node_modules\nicegui")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
